strategy_name: Pinocchio — long-wick pin bar after an established trend, trade against the wick
setup_summary: On a 1h or 4h chart, after an established trend (book shows an uptrend for the bearish version), a pin bar forms whose wick is at least 2x the size of its real body; trade the opposite direction of the wick (long upper wick after uptrend = short). The bar-level requirement is falsifiable: wick length >= 2 * body length, plus a prior-trend condition.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: long wick (>2x body) appearing after a trend. Invalidated/blocked if the market is neutral/choppy — a valid signal must come after a trend ('Trying to trade the bearish Pinocchio pattern in neutral market conditions can be risky'); also do not use a very short (60-sec) horizon.
risk_geometry: Entry: either immediately after the pin bar closes or as a limit at the 50% Fibonacci retracement of the pin bar's range (a limit-entry variant). Expiry 5-15 min in binary terms → expiry_bars in V8. No stop/target given in the book.
quote: A Pinocchio bar is a candlestick bar that has a very small body and a very long wick (nose)... when the wick is longer than the body, this tells us that the market is deceiving us and that we should trade the opposite way!
chapter_anchor: Strategies #2: The Pinocchio Strategy
mechanism: An outsized wick at the end of a trend shows the push was rejected, implying exhaustion of the directional move; the market then reverses toward the body/close side.
notes: Directly transferable to BTCUSDT 1h wicks (wick/body ratio needs an ATR-relative or fixed-ratio measure). Caveat: crypto wicks are frequently liquidation cascades rather than deliberate rejection, so the prior-trend requirement is load-bearing. The claimed 68% win rate in the book has no statistical backing. The 50% fib-retrace limit entry variant maps to a limit-entry option in risk_geometry.

strategy_name: 1-2-3 trend reversal — failed higher high confirmed by a break of the prior swing low
setup_summary: After an uptrend or strong move up, mark the first peak (1); if a counter-move begins, mark its bottom (2); if the next up-move fails to exceed point 1 and turns down, mark its high (3). Enter short only when price breaks below the point-2 low. All conditions are observable on the pattern timeframe: lower high (3<1) then structure break.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: complete 1-2-3 swing structure (lower high after a peak) plus a close below the point-2 swing low. Invalidated if price reverses back above point 3, or if point 3 exceeds point 1 (no lower high → no pattern).
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close through the point-2 low. Expiry set equal to the pattern timeframe; book risk rule: 'better to open two trades with smaller expiry times than 1 trade with longer expiry times' — a risk/lifecycle rule preferring split shorter-horizon exposure over one long-horizon bet. No stop/target given.
quote: If the new move up does not surpass point 1 and starts turning down, mark the highest point of this new move up with (3)... the price must move down to break the low created at point (2). If that happens, all our conditions are met, and we enter the trade with a 'Put'.
chapter_anchor: Strategies #3: The 1-2-3 Strategy
mechanism: A failed higher high signals weakening of the prior trend; the subsequent break of the intermediate swing low confirms trend reversal and provides a clean structure-defined trigger.
notes: Swing-point labeling (points 1-3) can reuse V8's windowed-extreme machinery. The 'two shorter trades over one long trade' rule is a candidate risk_rule/lifecycle_rule for V8 (exposure splitting by horizon) distinct from the one-exposure-per-direction invariant. Symmetric long version implied for downtrends, though the book only draws the bearish case.

strategy_name: Higher-timeframe trend confirmation — confirm trend one or two levels above the execution timeframe
setup_summary: Methodology rule: use a candlestick chart of a bigger timeframe than the expiry/execution timeframe to confirm the trend — at least 1h for pattern recognition, and 1h/4h to confirm the view when trading 15-30 min horizons; the 1-min chart gives entry/exit signals while 15-min and hourly charts confirm trend and support/resistance. Also 'use hourly chart to understand the underlying trend' even for the shortest 60-sec horizon.
trigger_invalidation: Not a directional setup; it prescribes the TF hierarchy: entry signals on the execution TF must be aligned with trend context on the next 1-2 TFs up. Falsifiable as a filter: entries taken without higher-TF trend alignment are the negative case.
risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target. Methodological constraint on signal validity, not a position geometry rule.
quote: In order to confirm a trend, use a candlestick chart with a bigger time frame than the one you use to decide your expiry time. it is usually recommended to use a time frame of at least 1 hour for chart pattern recognition.
chapter_anchor: Fundamentals — Expiry time: What time-frame to use for the pattern recognition
mechanism: Short-horizon price action is noisy; requiring the entry-timeframe signal to align with trend context on a higher timeframe raises the prior probability of continuation and filters counter-trend noise.
notes: Directly supports the existing trend_pullback expert's trend requirement and motivates a MarketState design where trend is computed on the confirmation TF (1-2 levels above the entry TF) as a PIT feature, reinforcing the no-wal-clock / PIT discipline. This is a lesson reinforcing architecture, not a new expert.

strategy_name: Triple Screen multi-timeframe trend confluence
mechanism: countertrend exhaustion within a dominant higher-timeframe trend reverts to the trend direction
setup_summary: Identify the trend on the timeframe one order of magnitude above the trading chart (factor ~5, e.g. weekly for daily, 4h/1d for a 1h trading chart) using EMA slope and/or MACD-Histogram slope; trade only in that direction or stand aside. On the trading chart, enter countertrend pullbacks when a short-term oscillator (5-day Stochastic, or 2-day EMA of Force Index) is oversold (long) or overbought (short); entry is a stop order above the prior day's high (long) or below the prior day's low (short). The higher-timeframe screen acts as a censor that removes one of the three choices (buy, sell, stand aside).
trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalidates if the higher-timeframe trend gate flips (weekly MACD-Histogram/EMA slope reverses); countertrend oscillator entries must be refreshed, never chased when already extended; entering when both timeframes trend the same direction is discouraged as 'hopping aboard a moving train'.
risk_geometry: Entry: buy-stop above the prior trading-chart bar high (long) or sell-stop below the prior bar low (short), or a limit placed at the depth of the average of recent penetrations below the EMA; stop: in the vicinity of the latest swing low/high; target: the opposite channel line (the book uses a channel containing 90-95% of recent prices); expiry: governed by the higher-timeframe trend gate.
quote: The Triple Screen trading system begins by identifying the trend on a chart one order of magnitude greater than the one you are planning to trade.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 7 (Trading Systems), Q 7-2, 7-5 to 7-9; Answers 7-2, 7-6, 7-8; also Answer 4-7
notes: Canonical Elder multi-timeframe system; the factor-of-5 timeframe rule is directly transferable to 24/7 perp crypto (e.g. 1h trading chart with 4h or 1d gate). Maps onto V8's trend_pullback expert as a refinement: add a higher-timeframe trend gate (EMA/MACD slope) and a short-term oscillator trigger, with a buy-stop above the prior bar high. Book explicitly states the purpose is to resolve conflicting timeframes, which matches V8's multi-clock/regime discipline.

strategy_name: Failed breakout / failed test of range border reverses
mechanism: A failed test of the trading-range border (resistance or support) shows the controlling side lacks momentum, so price is most likely to move in the opposite direction; a failed breakout above resistance often carries price all the way through the opposite border.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: after price breaks above a windowed resistance level and then closes back below it within N bars (failed breakout), expect movement in the opposite direction — enter SHORT on the failed-breakout bar close with the prior high frozen as reference; mirror for a failed test of support (LONG). The China Railway example generalizes the book's rule: a failed upside breakout preceded a strong move that broke through the opposite border (support).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close pierces the frozen range border then closes back inside the range within N bars. Invalidation: close re-crosses and holds beyond the failed border (thesis dead); the book also warns any breakout can 'reverse so that prices return to the established trading range', so a false-failure re-breakout must kill the trade.
risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE on the failure bar; stop just beyond the frozen prior_high/prior_low ref; target 1.0R+ toward the opposite range border; expiry in bars; still_valid = close stays on the failure side of the frozen ref.
quote: A failed test of resistance or support is most likely to lead to price movement in the opposite direction.
chapter_anchor: Part 1 Seg 1 (technical indicator areas); Part 2 Seg 4 (resistance and support; China Railway failed breakout)
notes: Directly corroborates the active failed_breakout expert (SHORT variant). Book adds the proximity principle (signals at range borders are strongest) and the double/triple top = repeated failed resistance tests as variants of the same family. No statistical support given; reliability asserted by practitioner narrative.

strategy_name: MA-touch mid-trend entry (pullback to rising average)
mechanism: In a confirmed uptrend with the moving average below price, a pullback that touches the rising MA is a low-risk continuation entry because the MA acts as dynamic support where the controlling side resumes.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h with an established uptrend (price above rising MA; trend confirmed by another indicator), when price falls and touches the rising slow MA, enter LONG on the next bar close; the book further requires uptrend confirmation and recommends treating the touch as an add-to-position point. Exit signal: when the MA crosses above price / curls, the uptrend is likely over and the position should be closed.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: MA below price, price dips to the MA, uptrend still confirmed. Invalidation: MA line moves through and above price (book: 'sold the entire position... wait for new signals'), or the retracement exceeds the pullback swing low.
risk_geometry: entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after MA touch; stop below the pullback swing low or an ATR multiple; target 1.0R+ or prior high; expiry in bars; still_valid = close holds above the rising MA.
quote: When MA is below price, as price falls and touches the MA, if the uptrend is confirmed, this point may be used to increase the size of the open position.
chapter_anchor: Part 8 Seg 4 (mid-trend entry, China Foods); Part 5 Seg 1 (20-day/200-day MA)
notes: Corroborates the active trend_pullback expert (ema_fast>ema_slow and close<ema_slow). The book frames the touch as continuation/add rather than entry, which is a risk-geometry variant V8 can test against the existing pullback trigger. Practitioner heuristic, no statistics.

strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement continuation zones
mechanism: After a primary impulse, counter-trend retracement tends to terminate at 23.6%/38.2%/61.8% of the impulse, after which the primary trend resumes; a reversal signal at a fib level marks the resumption point.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: after a measurable impulse leg (top-to-bottom extremes), compute 23.6/38.2/61.8% retracement levels of that leg; expect retracement to stall at one of them. Book procedure: look for a reversal signal at 23.6%, if none walk to 38.2%, then 61.8%; enter in the primary-trend direction only when a reversal signal actually appears at the level. No reversal signal anywhere in the pullback suggests it is a retracement, not a reversal.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pullback reaches a fib level AND an independent reversal signal prints there. Invalidation: price closes beyond the 61.8% level — the move is likely a trend change, not a retracement.
risk_geometry: entry on reversal-signal bar close at a fib zone; stop beyond the fib level; target trend continuation (next fib level or new extreme); expiry in bars; frozen impulse refs per PIT.
quote: Analysts expect retracement to occur at specific percentages against the prevailing trend. ... the key Fibonacci ratios of 23.6%, 38.2%, and 61.8%
chapter_anchor: Part 4 Seg 1 (Bollinger Bands and Fibonacci Retracement; Radio Shack examples)
notes: Fib levels are self-referential (no independent causal claim) but are widely watched, so they can serve as entry-zone features for the trend_pullback family rather than a standalone expert. Book folds this into the retracement-vs-reversal decision, which V8 encodes as a dead-thesis distinction.

strategy_name: Over-reaction swing fade (exaggerated move corrects in 1-3 sessions)
mechanism: Reactions to news/events are exaggerated and self-correct: the overshoot beyond the typical range is not a trend, and price reverts to the established range within one to three sessions.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: when a single session pushes price well outside its recent typical breadth (e.g., >N ATR excursion beyond a short-window range) or away from the established trading range, fade it — enter against the excursion and exit when price returns into the range, expecting completion within 1-3 sessions. The book's swing-timing rule: entry when price moves away from the typical daily breadth, exit on return to normal levels; this works best in moderately volatile names, poorly in highly volatile ones.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: excursion bar close beyond a frozen range threshold. Invalidation: no reversion into the range within the 1-3 session window (trend extension), or a second strong excursion bar in the same direction; book notes swing timing is hard in high-volatility issues.
risk_geometry: entry on excursion bar close; stop beyond the excursion extreme (or 1 ATR past it); target the range re-entry edge; expiry short (1-3 sessions per the book's correction window); still_valid = price has not broken to a new range.
quote: those exaggerated movements tend to self-correct within one to three trading sessions
chapter_anchor: Part 1 Seg 3 (random walk critique); Part 8 Seg 2 (swing timing; CA Inc. entry/exit examples)
notes: Leverage and liquidation cascades in perps generate frequent overshoot wicks, and the 24/7 no-gap tape makes the fade executable at the excursion close. This is the strongest mean-reversion candidate in the book for crypto. Distinct from bollinger_band_reversion (band-instrument trigger vs event/excursion trigger). The book's own caveat (fades work in 'isolated moments when price movement is extreme') supports gating this behind a volatility filter.

strategy_name: Volume spike as reversal warning / climax confirmation
mechanism: A single-session volume spike far above the typical range signals that the controlling side's conviction is exhausted, marking likely reversal when confirmed by price/momentum signals; volume 'precedes a strong reversal'.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: a session whose volume jumps far above the recent average (e.g., >Mx the 20-session mean) and then immediately returns to prior levels is a reversal warning — not a standalone entry, but a confirmation gate: 'exceptionally high volume in a single trading session is a key reversal warning', to be confirmed by price/candlestick/momentum. Book also defines the spike as non-recurring: volume returns to previous levels and does not repeat.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: volume > Mx windowed mean at/near a trend extreme or range border. Invalidation: spike without any price-pattern or oscillator confirmation (book repeatedly shows confirmed volume signals that failed); treat as no-signal rather than fade.
risk_geometry: no standalone geometry — a participation feature consumed as confirmation for candlestick/breakout candidates and as a trigger feature for the backlog capitulation family; volume comparison must be PIT (no future bars).
quote: exceptionally high volume in a single trading session is a key reversal warning. This should be confirmed by other indicators
chapter_anchor: Part 1 Seg 1; Part 6 Seg 1 (volume indicators; spike definition)
notes: Corroborates the DATA_BLOCKED capitulation backlog family (capitulation_exhaustion). Crypto caveat: volume must be aggregated across venues/derivatives tapes and taker-flow based; single-venue 1h volume is a biased proxy. Book gives no statistics — reliability claims are anecdotal.

strategy_name: ATR contraction as trend-slowdown early warning
mechanism: ATR measures conviction through session ranges; when range declines while the trend continues, the controlling side is losing enthusiasm and trend reversal is likely to precede other reversal signals.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: compute ATR(14) (or the windowed high-low range); if price keeps making trend-direction extremes but ATR contracts (declining slope over a window), the trend is slowing. The book's Exxon Mobil example: price shows no weakening but the strong ATR decline confirms likely near-term reversal. Operationally: a negative ATR-slope regime while a trend-following candidate is open should weaken/terminate that candidate.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: ATR slope negative over W bars while trend still extends. Invalidation: ATR slope flattens/rises (momentum rebuilding) or price breaks the range decisively (ATR contraction then expansion on the same side = continuation).
risk_geometry: no entry — a lifecycle/regime rule: candidate dead-thesis (still_valid=false) or size/heat reduction for trend_pullback-type experts when the volatility contraction condition holds; frozen ATR window per PIT.
quote: If the range begins to decline as the trend evolves, it provides a forecast that the trend may be slowing down. This 'early warning' often precedes other reversal or momentum signals.
chapter_anchor: Part 6 Seg 1 (ATR; Exxon Mobil example)
notes: Cleanly falsifiable: it is a pure function of the price tape already in MarketState (volatility group). This gives V8 a deterministic still_valid refinement for trend-pullback episodes without adding a new active expert. Book asserts ATR ranges rise with 'enthusiasm'; no statistics given.

strategy_name: Oscillator divergence as leading weakness signal
mechanism: When price and a momentum oscillator diverge (price new high, oscillator lower high), the trend is not confirmed and is probably weak; divergence acts as a leading warning that reversal confirmation should be sought.
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: price makes a new high while RSI(14) makes a lower high (bullish divergence = uptrend weak), or price makes a new low while RSI makes a higher low (bearish divergence = downtrend weak). Book rule: divergence alone is a warning to look for confirming price-pattern/candlestick exit or entry signals — 'The failure of RSI to confirm the new high levels in the price movement was the revealing signal that the trend was losing its momentum.' Divergence is most meaningful when it occurs near overbought/oversold extremes (RSI 70/30).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: new price extreme paired with a non-confirming oscillator extreme over the lookback window. Invalidation: oscillator re-confirms price (convergence) or crossover absent — book explicitly warns leading indicators give false whipsaw signals; divergence at mid-range is weaker than divergence near extremes.
risk_geometry: no standalone entry — a confirmation/gating feature (response group) for candlestick and Western reversal candidates; trigger requires the extreme window to be frozen per PIT.
quote: Bullish divergence means that an uptrend is not confirmed by the oscillator, in which case the uptrend is probably weak.
chapter_anchor: Part 6 Seg 2 (convergence and divergence; Wal-Mart example); Part 7 Seg 1 (RSI)
notes: On fast 1h crypto tape, RSI divergence is noisy and the book itself flags whipsaw/false-signal risk for leading indicators — so V8 should use it only as a confirmation input, never a standalone trigger. No statistics; the book frames divergence as 'rare enough that when it does appear, it should not be ignored.'

strategy_name: Pyramiding / position scaling on continuation
mechanism: Increasing position size on confirmed continuation (at retracement end, breakout-with-continuation, or MA touch) increases profit potential; the added exposure also increases loss risk proportionally.
setup_summary: The book's three timing methods for adding size: (a) add at the recognized end of a retracement; (b) add when price breaks out of the trading range with continuation signals (flip confirms new support); (c) add when price in an uptrend touches the rising MA. The book is explicit that this 'contradicts most technical assumptions of fixed position size' and that 'when open positions are increased, a greater risk of loss also occurs.'
trigger_invalidation: N/A as an active V8 strategy: conflicts with V8 rule 16 (one active exposure per instrument+direction). The compatible subset is partial-profit tranche exits (sell 1/10 per +5% increment) which is a lifecycle exit variant, not new exposure.
risk_geometry: would require adding exposure units to the ExposureBook mid-episode; each added unit needs its own stop/target; rule-16 change would require a registry decision with an authority receipt.
quote: Techniques for increasing position size are called pyramid systems or pyramiding. ... when open positions are increased, a greater risk of loss also occurs.
chapter_anchor: Part 8 Seg 4 (mid-trend entry; pyramid systems; greed and panic)
notes: Pyramiding violates the one-exposure-per-direction invariant; it can only enter V8 through a registry experiment that beats the single-exposure baseline on frozen OOS, per rule 16. The partial-profit-tranche exit, however, is compatible today as a lifecycle exit variant and is explicitly in the book ('set two exit points for any position... grows by 5%, one-tenth of the position will be closed').

strategy_name: Double Bollinger Band trend/range regime filter
mechanism: Price confinement between the 1-SD and 2-SD Bollinger bands indicates an active trend; confinement inside the 1-SD bands indicates a range, so band-zone residence discriminates trend vs range regimes and their direction
setup_summary: On daily charts, plot two sets of Bollinger Bands (20-period center MA, one at 1 SD and one at 2 SD, excluding center lines). When a pair closes the NY session (4pm ET) between the upper 1-SD and 2-SD bands it is in an uptrend; between the lower 1-SD and 2-SD bands, a downtrend; confined within the 1-SD bands = range. Only band-zone residence is a tradable trend state; when all four bands converge the pair is range trading.
trigger_invalidation: A daily close that exits the trend zone back inside the 1-SD (range) zone signals trend exhaustion; corroborating filter: ADX above 25 and rising confirms trend, ADX falling below 25 implies exhaustion/range.
risk_geometry: No entry/stop on the filter itself; it feeds the retrace-in-trend, new-trend and exhaustion-reversal setups; trend-exhaustion signal = close outside the trend zone.
quote: If the currency pair is trading between the upper one and two standard deviation bands, it is in an uptrend, and if it was trading between the two lower bands, it is in a downtrend.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, 'Bollinger Band Basics' and 'Knowing When the Trend Has Exhausted'
notes: Corroborated in the same book by the ADX>25 trend filter (Chapter 7). For 24/7 crypto the 'NY session close' must be replaced by a fixed calendar bar close (e.g., 00:00 UTC) and band zones are computed on rolling windows; no exchange gaps but weekend volume drops must be tolerated.

strategy_name: Bollinger first-band pullback in trend (value entry)
mechanism: In an ongoing trend the mean-reverting pullback to the inner 1-SD band marks a value level where continuation participants re-enter
setup_summary: Daily chart. Uptrend established (price between upper 1-SD and 2-SD bands): wait for price to retrace to the upper 1-SD band, enter LONG on the daily close; stop slightly below the 15-period SMA. Downtrend: wait for rally to the lower 1-SD band, enter SHORT on the close, stop slightly above the 15-day MA. Do not take the trade if the candle closes outside the band.
trigger_invalidation: A close outside the relevant band invalidates the entry; if the pair closes out of the trend zone entirely, the trend thesis is broken.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close (book: daily NY 4-5pm EST close); stop: beyond 15-day SMA; T1 = conservative 30-60 pips, exit half, move stop to breakeven; trail remainder (30-pip trailing stop); T2 further away; positions typically held overnight.
quote: In an uptrend, the way to find value is to wait for the currency pair to dip and retrace to the upper first standard deviation Bollinger Band. At that point, if we were looking to join the trend, we could go long with a stop placed slightly below the 15-day Simple Moving Average.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, 'Finding Value within a Trend'
notes: Anecdotal hit evidence: 8 value buys in a June-July 2010 GBP/USD uptrend, prior trend continued in all but one (small sample). This is a refinement/variant of the existing trend_pullback family: the BB 1-SD band replaces the ema_fast>ema_slow cross as the pullback definition and the stop is the 15-period SMA instead of an ATR multiple; for crypto 'daily close' becomes a fixed-UTC bar close.

strategy_name: New-trend entry on close into the outer band zone
mechanism: A daily close out of the range zone into the 1-SD-to-2-SD band zone marks the start of a new trend that tends to persist for days, but a first occurrence may only be a 24-hour continuation
setup_summary: Daily chart, close of the session. When a pair that was confined inside the 1-SD range zone closes into the uptrend zone (upper 1-SD to 2-SD bands) enter LONG; a close into the lower zone enter SHORT. Book records both a one-day failed continuation and a repeat close that produced a near-month-long trend, so the entry is taken each time but always managed with T1-T2.
trigger_invalidation: If the pair moves ~60 pips against entry it has re-entered the range zone and the new-trend thesis failed (book: when a trade went against her by more than 60 pips it was stopped 97% of the time).
risk_geometry: Entry: session-close bar; stop: 60 pips fixed (refined from 70; the 'sweet spot' for this setup); T1 = 30-60 pips on half, stop to breakeven; trail remainder; positions held 1-12 hours, sometimes overnight with stop and both targets set; book also refuses pairs with spread wider than 6 pips.
quote: At some point it had to get into the bands first, and the point where it enters the uptrend or downtrend zones creates an opportunity to join a new trend that could be emerging. When the currency pair ends the NY session (4 p.m. Eastern Time) within the first and second bands, there is a reasonable chance that it will remain within the bands for days to come.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, 'Getting into a New Trend'; Chapter 14 Lesson 1 & 2 (spread and stop refinement)
notes: Includes a rare empirical refinement from the book's own trade log (Chapter 14): a 60-pip stop adopted because >60 pips adverse correlated with a 97% stop-out rate, and a 6-pip spread admission cap. For V8 the 60-pip absolute stop becomes an ATR-relative or fixed-R parameter; the spread cap informs the simulator cost model.

strategy_name: News-surprise momentum with the 5-minute rule
mechanism: A large economic data surprise (actual vs forecast) triggers directional continuation after an initial noise burst; entering on a 5-minute candle close aligned with both the surprise and the prevailing trend raises the probability of continuation
setup_summary: Before a scheduled high-impact release (employment reports, retail sales, ISM/PMI, GDP, CPI/PPI) verify: (1) the data is high-impact; (2) the surprise is large (rule of thumb >5% vs forecast, sometimes 2% suffices; let price confirm); (3) sentiment alignment. Wait 5 minutes after release, then enter only if the 5-minute candle closed in the surprise direction AND price is on the corresponding side of the 50-period SMA on the 5-minute chart. If the first 5-minute candle closes against the data-consistent direction, the trade is void.
trigger_invalidation: 5-minute candle closes opposite to the surprise = no trade; good data but price below the 50-SMA (or vice versa) = sentiment overrides, skip; spreads start widening 5-10 minutes pre-release, so avoid that entry window.
risk_geometry: Entry: 5-min close after the 5-minute wait; stop: high/low of the data candle (for shorts/longs), minimum 20 pips, default 30-35 pips; T1 = amount risked (example: 31 pips), exit half, trail remainder 20-30 pips; first target usually hit within the first hour.
quote: The key is to wait five minutes before getting into the trade to make sure that the currency responds the way that it is supposed to.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 9, 'Sifting through the Headlines' and 'How Fast and Furious Trading Works'
notes: Crypto analog: US CPI/FOMC/NFP and similar macro releases move BTC, so the mechanism transfers, but microstructure differs - perps are 24/7 with millisecond reactions, no retail-broker spread widening, and liquidation cascades instead of stop clustering. Requires a macro-calendar feed as a response-group feature (event/available clock discipline). A second anecdote (USD/CAD, Chapter 9) shows the 5-minute rule filtering out a data-consistent trade that then failed.

strategy_name: Interest-rate / carry differential following
mechanism: Investors move capital toward the higher-yielding currency, driving its value up while it is funded by low-yield currencies; in risk-off episodes they unwind, selling high-yield and buying low-yield, so the carry trend flips with risk appetite
setup_summary: Long the high-yield currency funded by the low-yield one while risk appetite is on (the book's example: AUD above USD for most of 2010 because Australian rates exceeded US rates). Direction of rates matters more than level - a low-rate country can attract money if its rates are headed up. Unwind (short high-yield / long low-yield) when risk aversion rises, since carry unwinds move currencies in lockstep with equities.
trigger_invalidation: A central-bank policy path reversal, or a risk-off episode (sharp equity sell-off) that unwinds carry before the rate differential itself changes.
risk_geometry: Book gives no entry/stop specifics; multi-day-to-months hold; the stated risk control is position sizing because at 10:1 leverage a 10% adverse move wipes the account.
quote: If I had to pick only one thing to determine where currencies are headed, it would certainly be interest rates.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, 'Interest Rates' and 'Yield'; Chapter 5, 'The Direction of Interest Rates'
notes: For crypto perps the analog is the funding rate: positive-funding regimes behave like carry and funding-carry is a candidate strategy. There is no sovereign yield curve in perps, so this is a feature-group input (flow/funding) and a possible backlog strategy, not an immediate expert. Chapter 12 confirms the fragility: a carry-trade-only system worked 2001-2007 and crashed in 2008.

strategy_name: T1-T2 partial-profit / breakeven / trail exit method
mechanism: Banking half the position at a conservative first target roughly equal to the risk and moving the remainder to breakeven converts floating profit into realized profit while a residual position captures trend continuation
setup_summary: For any position: set T1 approximately equal to the amount risked (example: risk 40 pips, T1 = 40 pips). Exit half at T1, move the stop to the entry (breakeven), and trail the remainder (book: 30-pip trailing stop ratcheted every 20 pips). The method is net-positive if the strategy wins 60-70% of trades even with a slightly negative per-trade expectation, because partial profits are banked and the trade cannot lose money after breakeven.
trigger_invalidation: The book argues strict 2:1 risk/reward targets are unrealistic: on a ~100-pip average daily range a 70-pip target (for a 35-pip stop) demands 70% of a day's move, and a 10-pip stop gets clipped by noise plus 2-3 pips of spread.
risk_geometry: T1 = risk amount; breakeven stop on remainder after T1; trailing stop 30 pips, ratchet every 20 pips; T2 further and achievable; applied to both BB new-trend entries (T1 30-60 pips) and news trades (T1 = risk).
quote: When the target is hit, I would close out half of the position and move my stop to breakeven on the remainder of the position. If the trade continues to move in my favor, then I will trail the stop to lock in more profits.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, 'Bag Your Winners Quickly'
notes: Directly actionable in the V8 lifecycle: partial fill at T1, breakeven move, trailing ratchet. The book explicitly rejects strict 2:1 R:R in favor of a high-hit-rate, per-trade-negative-edge model on psychological grounds - a falsifiable alternative to the current fixed target_r/stop_r geometry worth testing as a VARIANT of an existing family.

strategy_name: Bollinger trend-exhaustion reversal (band re-entry)
mechanism: When a trend dies the price usually reverts at least to the first SD band on the other side, so entering at the first band after the first exhaustion close gives a counter-trend reversion trade
setup_summary: Daily chart. In a downtrend (price between lower 1-SD and 2-SD bands), wait for the first close above the lower 1-SD band (exhaustion), then go LONG with a stop at the most significant near-term low; the reversion frequently extends to the upper 1-SD band. Symmetric: after an uptrend's first close below the upper 1-SD band, short with a stop at the most significant near-term high.
trigger_invalidation: Price remains inside the trend zone (no exhaustion close) = no setup; a fresh close beyond the band in the original trend direction invalidates the reversion.
risk_geometry: Entry: close above/below the first band; stop: most significant near-term swing low/high; target: far first band or T1-T2 with the 15-period SMA as a partial-exit reference; book notes the far band is often a few hundred pips away, so T1-T2 is preferred over a single distant target.
quote: A practical way to pick a bottom would be to wait for the currency pair to close above the lower first standard deviation Bollinger Band with a stop at the most significant near-term low.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, 'Knowing When the Trend Has Exhausted'
notes: Counter-trend, so it ranks below continuation families for V8's trend-favoring evidence base; the book itself frames trend-fading as the contrarian ('Jack Shephard') approach suitable only for range-style personalities. Uses the same band machinery as the regime filter, so it is cheap to add once band features exist.

strategy_name: High-probability setup checklist (five alignments)
mechanism: Converging alignment of trend quality, fundamentals, calendar risk, market sentiment, and key levels raises the conditional probability of a trend-continuation trade
setup_summary: Before any trend-continuation long/short, verify five questions: (1) the retracement is shallow, not deep - deep corrections raise the risk the trend breaks; (2) there is no fundamental reason (e.g., disappointing data) behind the dip; (3) the next 24 hours of scheduled data are expected to support the trade; (4) risk appetite supports it (e.g., no 300-point Dow plunge that would trigger follow-through selling in Asia); (5) key support/resistance levels will not stall the trade.
trigger_invalidation: A deep correction, a fundamental driver behind the move, adverse expected data, adverse sentiment, or a broken key level each veto the trade; when factors conflict, judgment decides weighting.
risk_geometry: N/A - pre-trade admission filter; also includes the instrument-selection judgment to express a country-data view through a pair less affected by the USD (e.g., CAD news via AUD/CAD or CAD/JPY when US data is co-released).
quote: The point is to have as many stars aligned in your favor as possible on your trades and not to expose it to unnecessary and amateur risks.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 10, 'Sticking with High-Probability Trades' and 'If You're a Short-Term Trader...'
notes: This is a candidate-vetting heuristic, not an executable expert: it informs how V8 combines feature groups for setup admission (the 'as many variables as possible' principle) and the idea that a data view should be expressed in the instrument least contaminated by other drivers - a principle for V8's perp universe where USD/BTC macro is the dominant confound.

strategy_name: 30-day moving average trend filter
mechanism: price trading above a trend-defining moving average signals demand accumulation, biasing continuation over reversal
setup_summary: On the daily (or higher) timeframe, when price moves above the 30-day moving average, establish a long bias toward gains; the MA acts as a trend regime filter for entry decisions rather than a standalone entry. Complemented by the book's rule to never trade against the established trend ('wait for a beneficial tendency').
trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid while price trades back below the 30-day MA; also 'don't play against the trend' - do not initiate counter-trend positions in the filtered direction.
risk_geometry: Book gives no entry/stop/target for this; treat as a regime filter only - entry/stop/target geometry is inherited from the underlying expert (e.g., trend_pullback).
quote: One of his favorite measures is the 30-day moving average. When prices move above that level, he's more inclined to bet on gains.
chapter_anchor: Section 05, How pros evaluate the market (Wang Bing, commodity trader)
notes: Single practitioner anecdote, no statistics. A price-vs-MA filter is instrument-agnostic and transfers directly to 24/7 BTCUSDT; V8 already consumes MA features in trend_pullback, so this is a cheap regime-filter variant. Folds in the companion tip 'Transactions against a trend usually result in loss. Wait for a beneficial tendency and then make your move!' (Section 08, tip 5).

strategy_name: Carry / interest-rate differential thesis
mechanism: capital flows toward the higher-yielding currency, so the policy-differential trend persists until central banks converge
setup_summary: Hold the currency of the faster-growing economy funded by the slower-growing one; central-bank policy divergence sustains the differential trend (the book's 2016-17 dollar rally is attributed to a Fed tightening while peers eased). For crypto perps the direct analog is the funding rate: hold the perp direction that receives funding while the differential persists.
trigger_invalidation: Carry edge decays when policy converges or the yield/funding differential compresses; the book gives no explicit invalidation metric.
risk_geometry: A holding-period strategy; P&L accrues from the differential rather than price direction - requires funding-rate (derivatives tape) data that V8 does not yet ingest.
quote: It is better to invest in the currency of a country that is growing faster and fund it with a currency of a country that is growing slower.
chapter_anchor: Section 01, Forex trading quick facts + Section 02, Central bank Policy divergence

strategy_name: Trend persistence / hold-winners discipline
mechanism: trends are self-reinforcing because each new follower's flow extends the move, so premature profit-taking truncates the edge and counter-trend entries lose
setup_summary: When holding a winning position in an established trend, resist closing early: 'trends last longer than they might seem' and they develop quickly because participation grows as traders follow. Let targets be structure-based and keep losers closed early ('close the unsuccessful ... early').
trigger_invalidation: Qualitative exit discipline, not a falsifiable entry signal; the herding-continuation claim is a candidate mechanism for the simulator/expert exit modeling.
risk_geometry: Exit-side lesson: keep target at structure rather than manual early close; complemented by 'don't hold unsuccessful positions open for a long time'.
quote: Trends last longer than they might seem at first! ... when trends start, they develop quickly because they are increased by the number of traders following them.
chapter_anchor: Section 08, 10 tips from the pros (tips 2, 9, 10)
notes: Motivational framing with no data. The herding/self-reinforcement mechanism is plausible on perps (funding + leverage flows add momentum), but the claim is qualitative; useful as an exit-behavior hypothesis and a simulator lesson, not a standalone signal. Pairs with 'close unsuccessful positions early' and 'don't stop the profit'.

strategy_name: Multiple time frame context (higher TF trend, lower TF entry)
mechanism: higher-timeframe structure dominates lower-timeframe noise; a lower-TF signal read in isolation misreads routine pullbacks as reversals
setup_summary: Analyze 2-3 time frames spaced 4-8 bars apart (Month=>Week=>Day, or Day=>6h=>1h, or Day=>4h=>1h): the higher timeframe sets the trend (daily charts), the lower timeframe sets entry/exit (hourly). The book's worked example shows a daily downtrend that is a mere blip within a longer upward tendency - the canonical single-timeframe misread.
trigger_invalidation: Methodology, not a signal; applies to how any expert reads context on the 1h bar.
risk_geometry: None.
quote: For successful and precise market analysis, you must use at least 2-3 time frames! ... use daily charts to identify the overall trend and then use the hourly charts to determine specific entry levels.
chapter_anchor: Section 04, Multiple time frame analysis
notes: Directly relevant to V8's single-timeframe (1h) MarketState: a higher-TF trend context (e.g., 4h/1d trend feature) is a concrete, low-cost marketstate refinement candidate for the trend_pullback family and any regime filter. Practitioner consensus claim ('all good traders I know use 2-3 time frames'), no statistics.

strategy_name: Impulse System (EMA slope + MACD-Histogram slope alignment)
mechanism: when trend inertia (EMA slope) and momentum (MACD-Histogram slope) point the same way, the move is likely to continue until one leg flips
setup_summary: On the trading timeframe (1h for V8), go long when the EMA slope is rising AND the MACD-Histogram is above its prior bar and rising together; short when both are falling together. Clusters of same-direction signals carry more weight, and a higher-timeframe uptrend (weekly-equivalent) adds extra weight to bullish clusters. Falsifiable: both slope signs are computable from price; entry on the next bar after a confirmed cluster.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = EMA slope up + MACD-Histogram rising together (or both falling for short). Thesis invalidated when either component flattens or flips; book: 'both EMAs turn down, canceling the buy signal altogether.'
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close on signal cluster; stop below recent swing low (week's low on daily scale); the book advises tightening stops when the trend gets old and MACD-Histogram weakens.
quote: Buy signals emerge when both the EMA and MACD-Histogram are rising together; sell signals emerge when both are falling.
chapter_anchor: Part Two, Answers 54-56; also Trade 4/8 entry answers
notes: Distinct from V8 trend_pullback: this is a momentum-alignment entry rather than a price pullback. Heavily corroborated by the 8 case studies, which award points for 'Impulse buy' signals. A candidate new family once the active-expert budget allows.

strategy_name: Buy the pullback to a rising EMA (value trade); sell near the upper channel
mechanism: prices oscillate around value; buying near the rising EMA (value) and selling above value (channel wall) harvests the oscillation inside a trend
setup_summary: In an uptrend (rising EMA slope), buy when price pulls back into the value zone at/near the rising EMA ('sweet zone' between fast and slow EMAs); the book's entry is a limit order placed at the projected next-bar EMA value. Take profits when price touches the upper channel/envelope wall. Stop below the recent swing low (week's low on the daily scale).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = pullback into rising EMA in a confirmed uptrend. Invalidate = EMA flattens or turns down ('both EMAs turn down, canceling the buy signal'); stop hit.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit at projected next-bar EMA (book: 'estimate tomorrow's EMA value each day and place a buy order there'), or bar-close near EMA; stop: below recent swing low / week's low; target: upper channel line (a well-drawn channel contains ~95% of recent prices).
quote: Buying near the rising EMA is a value trade... If we buy near the moving average, near value, then our goal is to sell when the stock or commodity becomes overvalued, near the upper channel line.
chapter_anchor: Answers 27, 28, 30, 59; Trade 2 (SUNW) and Trade 7 (IBM) exit answers
notes: Directly corroborates V8 trend_pullback. Two concrete refinements: (a) limit-entry at projected next-bar EMA value instead of NEXT_BAR_CLOSE; (b) channel-wall target (EMA-anchored envelope) as an alternative to fixed target_r. In 24/7 crypto the daily bar is a 24h aggregation; EMA projection has no session dependency.

strategy_name: False breakout / no-follow-through reversal
mechanism: penetrating a significant extreme without follow-through exposes a vacuum of resting orders on the original side, so price reverts into the range
setup_summary: When price penetrates a significant prior extreme (new low / new high) but fails to follow through and closes back inside within a short window, trade the reversal: buy a false downside breakout, short a false upside breakout. Book examples: wheat penetrated a historic low and 'ticked up instead'; BVF took out its July low with 'no follow-through.'
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = penetration of a prior extreme with no follow-through (close back on the original side). Invalidate = follow-through continues through the level; close beyond the swept extreme.
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close after failed breakout; stop beyond the failed-breakout extreme ('tight stop immediately below the latest lows'); target = return into range / opposite channel wall.
quote: Wheat failed to follow through on that downside breakout and ticked up instead.
chapter_anchor: Trade 5 (Wheat) entry answer; Answer 21 ('a false upside breakout B was followed by a false downward breakout D'); Trade 8 (BVF) entry answer
notes: Corroborates V8 failed_breakout (SHORT variant). The book adds the mirror long side and an explicit short timing window ('within a week'). Crypto has no exchange gaps, so penetrate-and-reclaim is cleaner to detect on 1h bars.

strategy_name: Indicator/price divergence reversal (MACD-Histogram, MACD-lines, Force Index)
mechanism: a shallower indicator extreme against a deeper price extreme shows the driving side is exhausting, so the price move is due to reverse
setup_summary: Bullish divergence: price makes a lower low while the indicator (MACD-Histogram, MACD-lines, or Force Index) makes a higher bottom — buy. Bearish divergence: price makes a higher high while the indicator makes a lower top — sell. A confirmed higher-timeframe divergence is strong enough to override a declining EMA trend signal.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = divergence completes (indicator ticks up from a higher bottom at a lower price low, or ticks down from a lower top). Invalidate = the indicator confirms price by printing a new extreme ('if Stochastic does not turn up... it will confirm the strength of the downtrend').
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close after divergence confirmation; stop below the recent swing low (month's low in the case studies); 2% risk sizing applied on top.
quote: Divergences are the strongest signals of MACD-Histogram... a bullish divergence of MACD-Histogram allowed us to override the signal of the EMA.
chapter_anchor: Answers 32-33, 35, 39; Trade 1 (ORCL) and Trade 5 (Wheat) entry answers
notes: 'Strongest signals' is asserted, not statistically demonstrated. Divergence is an early-signal trade that whipsaws in persistent crypto trends, so pair it with the higher-timeframe trend-override gate. Needs frozen prior-extreme refs like existing V8 experts.

strategy_name: Elder-ray countertrend power exhaustion (Bear/Bull Power tick)
mechanism: in a trend, the countertrend side exhausting its power (Bear Power negative then ticking up in an uptrend) marks the pullback's end and a resumption entry
setup_summary: In an uptrend (EMA slope up), buy when a bar's low pierces below the EMA (Bear Power = low − EMA becomes negative) and Bear Power then ticks upward; in a downtrend, short when Bull Power (high − EMA) rises to or above zero and then ticks down.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = countertrend power negative then ticking up (long) / Bull Power ticking down from zero (short). Invalidate = EMA slope flips, or the countertrend power keeps printing new extremes (trend is breaking, not merely pulling back).
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close on the tick; stop beyond the signal bar's extreme (below the bar's low for longs); target = upper channel line (sell above value).
quote: When the trend, identified by the slope of the EMA, is up and Bear Power becomes negative but then ticks upward, it gives a buy signal.
chapter_anchor: Answers 36-37
notes: A concrete oscillator trigger for pullback-in-trend; could alternatively be implemented as an alternative trigger variant of trend_pullback rather than a standalone family. Fully falsifiable with EMA plus bar high/low.

strategy_name: Force Index (volume x price change) countertrend exhaustion entry
mechanism: a negative smoothed Force Index during an uptrend shows the pullback was driven by shrinking/one-sided selling that is exhausting, so the trend resumes
setup_summary: In an uptrend, buy when the 2-day EMA of Force Index (today−yesterday price change times today's volume) becomes negative; in a downtrend, sell when it turns positive. Force Index spikes identify exhaustion moves near reversal areas.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = smoothed Force Index crosses zero against the trend (negative in uptrend / positive in downtrend). Invalidate = the EMA trend flips.
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar close after the zero-cross; stop below the swing low; exit on Force Index spikes or at the channel wall.
quote: Force Index gives buy signals when it declines below zero during uptrends.
chapter_anchor: Answers 34-35
notes: Volume on crypto perps is exchange-reported and wash-trade-inflated, so the participation feature needs audit. Best framed as a volume-confirmed variant trigger for trend_pullback rather than a new family.

strategy_name: Opening-range breakout (narrow range expands; wide range caps the day)
mechanism: a narrow opening range concentrates participants and sets up an expansion; a wide opening range has already absorbed the day's flow and caps the day
setup_summary: Define the opening range (first ~30-60 minutes of the session). A narrow opening range tends to produce an important breakout; a wide opening range may set the day's high and low. In an established trend, a breakout from the opening range in the trend direction is the first high-quality intraday signal (book example: downside breakout from the opening range confirms a downtrend and gives the day's first short).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = price breaks the opening range in the trend direction. Invalidate = wide opening range (fade or stand aside); breakout fails and price returns into the range.
risk_geometry: Entry on range breakout; stop on the far side of the range; intraday target (channel / day's projection); day-trade only — no overnight risk.
quote: A wide opening range may define the high and the low of the day, but prices are likely to break out of a narrow opening range.
chapter_anchor: Answers 51-52, 56
notes: Crypto has no opening bell; anchor the reference range to the daily UTC open (funding-mark boundary) or a fixed session window on 1h bars. The same chapter's U-shaped intraday volume curve (Answer 51 — pros dominate near session close) is a flow/time feature input if a session is defined.

strategy_name: Morning/evening star three-bar reversal
mechanism: trend bar, then an isolated small-body bar showing indecision, then a strong counter-trend bar that closes well into the first bar's body = control handed over
setup_summary: Morning star (bottom): in a downtrend, a long black bar, then a small real body (spinning top or doji) that gaps away from the prior body (ideally no body overlap; shadow intrusion allowed), then a white bar closing well into the first black bar's real body. Evening star is the mirror in an uptrend (long white, isolated small body, black bar closing into the first body). Entry on the close of the third bar.
trigger_invalidation: Third bar fails to close well into the first bar's body (pattern incomplete); second (star) body overlapping the first body weakens/voids the pattern; opposite move beyond the third bar's extreme negates.
risk_geometry: Entry: close of the third bar. Stop: beyond the third bar's low/high (or pattern extremes). Target: structure. Volume rule: light volume on the first bar plus heavy volume on the third bar intensifies the signal.
quote: A long, black candle develops, assuring the bears that they continue to be in command. Then a small real body or spinning top appears, gapping down at the open... The final candle of the morning star pattern is a white real body that moves deeply into the first session's black candle.
notes: The 'gap away' between the star and the first body requires non-overlapping bodies, which is structurally rarer in continuous 24/7 perp markets than in exchange sessions. The doji-star variants (morning/evening doji star) overlap with the doji finding. Lower priority than hammer/engulfing.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Close-based break of support/resistance
mechanism: a close beyond a level reflects committed willingness to hold the price there, unlike an intraday poke; therefore break validity, window support, and S/R holding are all defined on closes
setup_summary: A break of resistance/support is only confirmed by a close above/below the level; an intraday break that closes back inside is not a break and is not a signal. A bar that dips below support but closes back inside the box range is 'not as bearish' - buyers returned before the close.
trigger_invalidation: A close back inside the range voids the break signal and keeps the level intact; the level is not dead until a close beyond it confirms.
risk_geometry: Methodology rule feeding V8's breakout_retest backlog and failed_breakout family: entry on the close-based break (NEXT_BAR_CLOSE), stop back beyond the level, dead-thesis on close back inside.
quote: An intraday break of support or resistance does not have the same significance as a severing of support or resistance on a close... Resistance or support is not considered broken unless by a close.
chapter_anchor: Ch1 S3 (p.22) + Ch4 Trading Guidelines (p.122)
notes: Directly reinforces V8's failed_breakout (close below windowed prior high) and the close-based semantics already in the spec. In 24/7 crypto the 'close' is the 1h bar close; no exchange-gap nuance applies.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Major-trend direction filter for reversal signals
mechanism: reversal signals aligned with the major trend have better base rates; counter-trend reversal signals are exits or alerts, not new-position triggers
setup_summary: Initiate a new position on a bullish candle signal only when the major trend is up (e.g., signal arriving after a pullback to support in an uptrend); a bullish signal in a downtrend is used only to cover shorts or as an alert to sell the bounce. The more overbought/oversold the market, the more vulnerable it is to reversal.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - an admission gate; a violation means 'do not initiate', not invalidation of a position.
risk_geometry: Gate applied before risk_geometry construction (RiskGate-level admission rule); counter-trend signals remain usable for cover/exits, never for new entries.
quote: If you see a reversal signal, consider initiating a new position only if that signal is in the direction of the major trend... A bullish candle signal in a bear trend should be used either to cover shorts or as an alert that the market may rally and to use that rally to sell.
chapter_anchor: Ch1 S3 (pp.20-21) + Ch4 Guidelines (p.122)
notes: Strong candidate for a RiskGate admission rule or expert-level regime filter in V8. Note the book's softer definition of 'reversal' (up to neutral, not up to down) which aligns with V8's evidence-bound framing.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Mandatory risk/reward gate before any candle-signal trade
mechanism: even a perfect pattern is not a trade unless expected reward exceeds defined risk; candles provide no price targets, so targets must come from Western structure (pivots, trend lines)
setup_summary: For any candle-signal trade: define risk as entry close to stop (e.g., under the hammer low), define the target from structure (prior high, falling resistance line, pivot). Skip the trade when risk approx equals reward (book example: $2 risk vs $2 target = no trade); only take it when the R multiple is attractive (book's worked hammer example accepts 1:2.5).
trigger_invalidation: N/A - a gate, not a signal.
risk_geometry: This gate is what produces V8's target_r/stop_r pairs; it explicitly recommends skipping ~1:1 setups and taking the trade only when reward exceeds risk. Risk measured from the signal bar's close to the stop ref; target from location features.
quote: NEVER PLACE A TRADE WITH A CANDLE SIGNAL UNTIL YOU HAVE CONSIDERED THE RISK/REWARD OF THE POTENTIAL TRADE... Bullish hammer or not, if the risk is $2 and the target is also $2 from the hammer's buy signal, this is not a trade that warrants action.
notes: Corroborates V8's risk_geometry spec and its 'no economic claim without a gate' philosophy. Two limitations stated by the book: candles do not give price targets, and no signal should be traded standalone - targets come from location features (prior pivots, trend lines).
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Hanging man top with next-bar close-under confirmation
mechanism: a hammer-shaped bar after an uptrend shows an intraday sell-off that was bought back; longs who entered near the close are vulnerable, and a next-bar close under its real body traps them, risking a cascade of selling
setup_summary: After an uptrend (preferably at or near the high of the move), a bar forms with a small real body at the top of the range, little or no upper shadow, and a lower shadow at least 2x the real body - the same shape as a hammer but in an uptrend. Do not short on the pattern bar: only short on a subsequent bar that closes under the hanging man's real body.
trigger_invalidation: No confirmation close under the hanging man's real body = no sell signal (the book's worked exhibits explicitly conclude 'we did not get any sell signals'); a close above its high negates.
risk_geometry: Entry: close of the confirming bar (the close under the hanging man's real body). Stop: above the frozen hanging-man high. Target: structure. This is a trigger-lag design: the entry fires on a confirmation close, not on the pattern bar close.
quote: For the hanging man's bullish long lower shadow one must wait for a close under the hanging man's real body before becoming bearish... if the market closes lower the next day, those who bought on the close of the hanging man day are now left 'hanging' with a losing position.
chapter_anchor: Ch2 S1 (pp.30-31, 40), Ch4 Guidelines (p.122)
notes: Directly informs V8 trigger semantics: some candle reversals require a confirmation bar (entry on the confirmation close / NEXT_BAR_CLOSE), not the pattern bar itself. This is a lifecycle/trigger design lesson generalizable to doji and high-wave tops.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Small real bodies / long-shadow series as trend-losing-force alert
mechanism: shrinking real bodies and mounting rejection shadows show the controlling side can no longer sustain closes at the extremes, so the prior trend is losing force
setup_summary: During an ascent, a series of small real bodies (spinning tops) or long upper shadows implies the bulls do not have full control - a warning not to follow longs, and near overextension/resistance a reversal may be forming. During a descent, a series of long lower shadows implies the bears lack full control. Inside a box range these carry no signal (there is no trend to reverse).
trigger_invalidation: No trade implication inside a box range; a single small body alone is insufficient - it is a contextual alert, not an entry signal.
risk_geometry: No entry geometry; used to scale back existing positions, defer entries, or gate continuation (e.g., do not add longs in a channel showing consecutive long upper shadows).
quote: If there are small real bodies (either black or white) during an ascent, caution is warranted from the long side... Such spinning tops are a warning not to follow this market from the long side... A series of long upper shadows as the market is ascending implies that the bulls do not have full control.
chapter_anchor: Ch2 S1 (pp.28-30) + Ch4 Trading Guidelines (p.121-122)
notes: Propose as marketstate features: small-body frequency and shadow-dominance ratios over a recent window, feeding exhaustion alerts or entry gating. Corroborates the existing 'trend losing force' concept already used informally in V8 design.
book: The Candlestick Course 2003

strategy_name: Volume-confirmed reversal patterns
mechanism: the force behind a reversal is credible only when volume dries up on the trend/pattern bar and expands on the confirmation bar; low-volume moves lack conviction and often fail
setup_summary: For a reversal pattern (engulfing, star, belt-hold), treat the signal as stronger when the first/trend bar prints light volume and the final/confirmation bar prints heavy volume (e.g., light volume on the black bar of a bullish engulfing plus a volume spike on the white turnaround candle; a belt-hold off support 'on strong volume' has more fuel).
trigger_invalidation: A confidence filter, not a standalone signal; absent volume data means a weaker signal, not an invalidation.
risk_geometry: Confidence filter on pattern-based entries; no geometry of its own.
quote: Light volume develops on the first candle line, followed by heavy volume on the third candle line. The light volume tells you that the force propelling the initial trend was weakening... Strong volume shooting into the third candle fuels the force that ignites the new trend.

strategy_name: Trend pullback (simple/shallow pullback)
mechanism: Markets thrust, correct, then resume; entering only on resumption avoids tops and false reversals
setup_summary: Strong uptrend (ADX>=30 and +DMI>-DMI, or Trend Qualifiers) that has made a two-month (~43-bar) new high; price then makes 3-7 consecutive lower highs (width) without retracing more than ~15% (shallow depth). Enter next bar on a trade 1/16 above today's high; protective stop 1/16 below the lowest bar of the pullback, capped at 5% of price.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price trades above the prior bar's high after a 3-7 bar pullback from a two-month high. Thesis invalidated: trade below the pullback low, or pullback exceeding ~50% retracement of the prior trend / width beyond ~7 bars (momentum negated).
risk_geometry: Entry: stop-order 1/16 above prior bar high (next-bar trigger, valid ~2 bars). Stop: 1/16 below lowest bar of the setup, capped at 5% risk if wider. Target: partial profits at 1R (2-for-1), trail remainder; typical holding 2-7 bars. Expiry: time-stop ~7 bars unless strong trend.
quote: The width should be wide enough so the market has enough time to correct but not too long as to negate the market's initial momentum. Three-to-seven bars is a good rule of thumb here.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, Pullbacks (pp. 33-58)
notes: Confirms the existing trend_pullback expert and adds concrete parameters: width 3-7 bars, shallow depth <=15%, two-month (43 trading-day) new-high location. The book also warns early pullbacks in a stair-step are superior to later ones. On BTCUSD 1h, 'trading day' maps to 1h bar; a two-month high is ~43*24=1032 bars, which is a viable frozen location reference.
book: Dave Landry on Swing Trading 2001

strategy_name: Deep pullback snapback (knee-jerk rebalance)
mechanism: A sharp deep pullback in a strong trend creates an out-of-balance situation; panicked shorts and shaken longs force a violent snap-back in the trend direction
setup_summary: Strong trend (ADX>=30 or Trend Qualifiers) with a two-month new high; then a sharp sell-off of >=15% (deep pullback) over 3-7 bars. Enter next bar 1/16 above today's high expecting a short, sharp knee-jerk snap-back toward the original trend.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above prior bar high after a >=15% deep pullback in a strong trend. Invalidation: trade below the setup low (stop); if the deep pullback does not reclaim quickly the 'snap-back' thesis is dead.
risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above prior bar high. Stop: book uses a fixed 5%-of-price stop for deep pullbacks (setup low often >8% away). Expected holding: short and sharp (days not weeks). Target: 2-for-1 scale-out, windfall capture on the parabolic move.
quote: Like a rubber band being stretched to extremes, the market often violently “snaps back” in the direction of the longer-term trend as shorts scramble to cover and longs jump back in.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5, Pullbacks - Snapbacks (pp. 46-51)
notes: Depth-threshold variant of the pullback family (a parameter variant = one multiplicity unit in V8), but with a distinct payoff profile: short sharp knee-jerk vs smooth longer continuation. Highly relevant to perps where leveraged longs get liquidated on deep 1h dips before mean reversion - falsifiable and screenable, not to be assumed.

strategy_name: Double Top Knockout (false-reversal continuation)
mechanism: A false double-top reversal attracts eager top-pickers and shakes out nervous longs; when the reversal fails, trapped traders' covering and re-entry fuel trend resumption
setup_summary: Strong trend; market makes a new two-month high; makes another new high no sooner than 3 bars later (allowing the false double top to form); then makes at least a two-bar low that 'confirms' the double top. Buy next bar 1/16 above today's high; stop 1/16 below yesterday's low (max 5%).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above today's high after the 2-bar low pullback from the second high. Invalidation: trade below the setup low; a genuine reversal would not trigger the buy-stop.
risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above today's high (next bar). Stop: 1/16 below yesterday's low, capped at 5%. Target: continuation above the double top; 2-for-1 management.
quote: Reversal patterns of markets in strong uptrends attract eager top pickers. These patterns also shake out the nervous longs. When the reversal fails to follow through, these players are trapped on the wrong side of the market or knocked out.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Fakeouts and False Moves - Double Top Knockout (pp. 68-74)
notes: Continuation-side complement to V8's failed_breakout: it buys the failure of a counter-trend reversal instead of shorting a failed trend breakout. Requires a two-month-high location feature. On BTC 1h the 'two-month calendar high' is a ~43-day windowed extreme - implement as a frozen reference.

strategy_name: Trend Pivot Pullback (false-rally shakeout re-entry)
mechanism: A one-day false rally inside a pullback shakes out fast money; re-entry above the failed rally high catches the true trend resumption
setup_summary: Strong trend; two-month new high; 1-5 lower highs; then a one-day rally (high greater than prior day's high) followed by a lower high, forming a pivot high. Buy tomorrow or next day 1/16 above this pivot high; stop 1/16 below the lowest bar in the setup (max 5%).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above the pivot high within 2 bars. Invalidation: trade below the setup low; pivot high must sit below the two-month high or it is not a pullback. Strictly safer than a Simple Pullback at the cost of missed fills.
risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above the pivot high, order valid 2 bars. Stop: 1/16 below lowest bar in the setup, max 5%. Target: resumption toward/through the old high; 2-for-1 scale-out.
quote: Trend Pivot Pullbacks seek to identify pullbacks that have had this false rally. This rally draws in, and subsequently shakes out the “fast money”—traders without staying power (money) and/or patience.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 6, Fakeouts and False Moves - Trend Pivot (False Rally) Pullbacks (pp. 75-81)
notes: Second-entry variant of the pullback family with a distinct trigger (pivot-high retest) that filters false first entries. On 1h crypto the pivot definition is bar-based and fully executable via a stop order above the pivot high.

strategy_name: Bow Tie (MA proper-order rollover with countertrend confirmation)
mechanism: Multiple moving averages converging then re-spreading marks a major trend-regime shift; entering only after a countertrend bar filters false starts
setup_summary: With 10-SMA / 20-EMA / 30-EMA: the averages converge and re-spread, shifting from proper downtrend order (10<20<30) to proper uptrend order (10>20>30) over ~3-4 days; then a lower low (longs) / higher high (shorts); buy next bar 1/16 above today's high; cancel the order if the market trades back to the 20-EMA.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above today's high after the countertrend confirmation. Invalidation: price trades back to the 20-EMA before fill - order cancelled (trend-shift thesis dead). Pulling back to the 10-SMA is considered normal/healthy.
risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above today's high. Stop: below lowest bar in the setup, max 5%. Target: new trend; 2-for-1 management; order-cancel rule tied to 20-EMA.
quote: In spite of what many books on technical analysis will tell you, moving-average crossovers do not work... You often avoid false moves by waiting for a countertrend by only entering if the trend re-asserts itself.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Bow Ties (pp. 83-91)
notes: Book explicitly rejects naive MA crossovers and requires countertrend confirmation - a methodological lesson for any MA-based family. Higher signal latency than pullback/knockout families; on 1h crypto the 10/20/30 convergence needs ~30+ bars of lookback. Could serve as a trend-regime-shift detector feeding other families.

strategy_name: High-Level Micro Double Bottom (continuation)
mechanism: In a strong trend, a brief two-pivot-low consolidation (micro double bottom) resolves upward; the twice-tested level becomes strong support
setup_summary: Strong trend (ADX>=30 or Trend Qualifiers) that has made a two-month high; the stock makes a pivot low (low surrounded by two higher lows), then another pivot low at or near the same level; buy next bar 1/16 above the high of the right side of the second pivot low; stop below the lowest bar of the setup (max 5%).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trade above the high of the second (right) pivot formation. Invalidation: trade below the setup's lowest bar; the two pivot lows must be at or near the same level.
risk_geometry: Entry: 1/16 above the right pivot high. Stop: below lowest bar of the setup, max 5%. Target: trend continuation; 2-for-1 management.
quote: We define the pattern as two pivot lows which form at or near the same level.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Micro Patterns - High-Level Micro Double Bottom (pp. 93-99)
notes: The book admits micro patterns are 'discretionary in nature,' so formalization requires a precise pivot-window definition (a low surrounded by two higher lows). The 'tested level becomes support' mechanism corroborates V8's location feature group and liquidity-sweep ideas.

strategy_name: Trend Qualifiers (multi-factor trend-strength composite)
mechanism: A composite of observable trend clues - base breakout, new two-month high/low, strong/weak closes, wide-range bars, gaps/laps with the trend, MA proper order/slope/daylight - indicates trend quality and trend direction
setup_summary: A market is in a strong uptrend when several qualifiers coincide: base breakout (wide-range bar after sideways), new two-month high, closes in the top 25% of range, range wider than prior 5 bars, gaps/laps in trend direction, 10-SMA>20-EMA>30-EMA with positive slope and 'daylight' (lows above the MAs). Standardized proxy: ADX>=30 with +DMI>-DMI. Markets trend only ~30% of the time.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - this is a filtering/methodology construct, not a standalone trade. Conflicting qualifiers (low ADX, no daylight, improper MA order) argue against trend-assuming entries; ADX>=25 for early trends vs >=30/35 for strong trends is the stated trade-off.
risk_geometry: No entry/stop/target. Used to gate admissible setups (trend filter) and for scanning: ADX>=30, historical volatility >=40%, 10-day avg volume >=100k, price >=$20-30, spread <=1/4 point.
quote: Strong Closes—When a stock closes within the top 25% of its range, it suggests that traders were willing to carry the position overnight.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 3, Trend Qualifiers (pp. 17-27); Chapter 4 Stock Selection (pp. 29-31); Appendix ADX (pp. 224-233)
notes: Direct input for V8's trend feature group: ADX/DMI, MA proper-order + slope + daylight, close-location-in-range, wide-range-bar, and new-high features. These can refine the trend qualification every trend-following expert consumes and act as a regime gate. 'Markets only trend about 30% of the time' is a regime-mix warning for any trend family.

strategy_name: Ideal Ichimoku confluence trend-following (foundation strategy)
setup_summary: On the reference timeframe (book: daily), LONG when (a) close is above the Kumo Cloud formed by Senkou A=(Tenkan+Kijun)/2 and Senkou B=52-bar midpoint, both shifted +26 bars; (b) Tenkan Sen (9-bar midpoint of high/low) > Kijun Sen (26-bar midpoint); (c) Chikou Span (close shifted back 26) is above price-from-26-bars-ago in 'open space'; (d) future Kumo bullish (future Senkou A > future Senkou B); (e) price within a bounded distance of Tenkan (200 pips) and Kijun (300 pips); (f) no Kumo shadow overhead and at least 50 pips of room to next resistance. Mirror for SHORT. Entry at next bar close or limit alert at resistance+buffer (40 pips).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = all five components aligned in one direction. Invalidation = close back into/through the Kumo Cloud, or Tenkan Sen crossing Kijun Sen against the position (trend change), or Chikou entering the cloud. Author's backtest shows trades last weeks-months and capture only ~30-50% of max profit (by design).
risk_geometry: Entry: next-bar close or limit above resistance/below support plus buffer (40 pips bullish, 35 bearish). Initial stop = Kijun Sen minus exit buffer; in 'Preserve mode' at +300 pips profit stop migrates to Tenkan Sen. Target: structure/alerts, no fixed R; expiry: none, trend trade. Gap risk acknowledged as reason stops are mandatory.
quote: Price has to be above Kumo Cloud; Tenkan Sen is greater than Kijun Sen; Chikou is showing strong bullish momentum ("Open Space"); There should be at least 50 pips to the next major support or resistance value; Kumo Future is bullish
chapter_anchor: Chapter 2 'Ichimoku Trading Plan' strategy description (pp.42-44); Chapter 5 'Ideal Ichimoku Strategy' (p.150)
notes: The five-component confluence is directly computable on 1h bars (26-bar Kijun ~= 26h window). 24/7 trading removes the weekend/close distortion the book frets about for FX, so bar counts are cleaner. The book supports it with a manual 2-year EURUSD daily backtest (8-11 trades, R/R improved from 1.51 to 0.88 after rule tweaks), but it is discretionary (alerts re-placed by eye, acknowledged errors), so DESIGN_INFERENCE not LITERATURE_SUPPORTED. The bounded-distance entry gate and preserve-mode exit are the load-bearing sub-rules to test.

strategy_name: Tenkan Sen/Kijun Sen crossover with cloud + momentum filters
setup_summary: Enter LONG at next bar close when Tenkan Sen (9-bar midpoint) crosses above Kijun Sen (26-bar midpoint), AND price is above a thin Kumo Cloud (or within ~50 pips below it for FX, accepting price will slice through a thin cloud), AND Chikou Span is in 'open space', AND price/Tenkan/Kijun/Chikou are not inside a thick cloud. Optional filters: future Senkou A >= future Senkou B and future cloud not thick. Mirror for SHORT. Book positions this as the Ichimoku analog of the 10/30 SMA crossover with a 200-SMA-style trend gate.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = TS/KS cross with thin-cloud + open-space conditions. Invalidation = cross back (TS recrosses KS against position) or price closes back through the cloud. Book shows this captures more of the trend than the ideal strategy but with more whipsaw ('you will learn the consequences as you backtest').
risk_geometry: Entry: next bar close at cross. Stop: Kijun Sen minus buffer (plan-dependent). Target: ~250-400 pips in the book's example trade; no fixed expiry. The book intentionally omits full money management for advanced strategies.
quote: If the 10 period SMA crosses over the 30 period SMA when price is above the 200 period SMA then a bullish trade is entered... The Tenkan Sen/Kijun Sen crossover strategy is similar to this strategy.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5 'Tenkan Sen/Kijun Sen Cross Strategy' (pp.150-154)
notes: A midpoint-of-high/low cross is a volatility-aware relative of an EMA cross; both TS/KS and ema variants can coexist as variants of one moving_average_cross family in V8's variant model. 24/7 bars make the 9/26 structure unambiguous. Note: author's least-favorite 'Kumo Cloud Breakout' is a separate strategy (see failed_breakout finding); do not merge.
