strategy_name: Chikou Span 'open space' momentum/regime filter
setup_summary: Compute Chikou Span = close shifted back 26 bars. Trend momentum is strong ('open space') when, projecting forward 5-10 bars, the Chikou line would NOT run into price-from-26-bars-ago either horizontally (price consolidates) or vertically (price moves 5-10%). If it would collide, momentum is weak and the trend is suspect. Usable as a regime gate on trend experts rather than a standalone entry.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = Chikou in open space (no collision within the forward 5-10 bar / 5-10% box). Invalidation = Chikou enters/collides with historical price, or Chikou crosses price-from-26-bars-ago (trend flip).
risk_geometry: No entry geometry; pure filter/feature. The book's 'visual square box' heuristic is a forward-looking probe, inherently look-ahead-free if computed only from the shifted series at time t.
quote: If the Chikou Span runs into price, then there is not much of a trend momentum... If the Chikou Span is in "open space" then the trend momentum is strong because today's price is not going to run into any price support/resistance from 26 periods ago.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 1 'Chikou Span' (pp.19-25)
notes: This is a falsifiable, look-ahead-free momentum feature: distance of the shifted close to historical price over a forward window. Maps cleanly to a history-group feature feeding trend experts (e.g. trend_pullback, ichimoku confluence). In perps, 26h and the 5-10% vertical probe are directly meaningful given 24/7 bars.

strategy_name: Kumo Cloud breakout with fake-break rejection (refinement of failed_breakout)
setup_summary: Book's 'Kumo Cloud Breakout Strategy': enter on close above (below) the Kumo Cloud with the same TS/KS/Chikou alignment filters. Author explicitly rates it weakest of the five strategies because close-throughs frequently reverse within the next bar or two ('fake' break of major S/R) - one observed pair of breakouts looked identical ex-ante, one ran 1,000 pips and one failed under 100. The cloud edge (esp. a long flat Senkou B or Kumo shadow behind price) is a well-defined, precomputed level usable as the prior-high/level reference for the existing failed_breakout family.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = close through cloud edge with alignment. Invalidation = close back inside/through the other side within 1-2 bars (fake break) -> stand aside or flip. The book's lesson: breakout signal alone is weak; confirmation (retest held) is required.
risk_geometry: Entry above cloud edge + buffer; stop below Kijun or below cloud; target prior extreme. No fixed expiry.
quote: there are many times where prices break out of the Kumo Cloud and then the next bar or bars reverse right away. It was basically a "fake" break of a major support or resistance.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 5 'Kumo Cloud Breakout Strategy' (pp.155-156)
notes: Directly corroborates the existing failed_breakout expert (mechanism liquidity_vacuum_reentry): fake breaks create the reentry short. The Kumo/Senkou B edge is a deterministic, frozen-reference candidate for the windowed prior-high ref; cloud thickness is a volatility-group input. In perps, close-through semantics and 1-2 bar reversal windows map to 1h bars.

strategy_name: Kijun-distance 'equalize' entry gate and extended-price retraction
setup_summary: Do not enter a trend trade while price is 'far' from the Kijun Sen (26-bar midpoint); wait for equalization. The book operationalizes 'far' as >200 pips from Tenkan / >300 pips from Kijun (fixed-pip, per instrument) and suggests a volatility-scaled alternative: price >= 1.5x ATR away from Kijun counts as far and historically preceded a pullback (Fig 1.24, June 8 2009). Conversely, when price is far from a FLAT Kijun, high probability of retraction to Kijun -> major pullback or trend reversal. A 2-year backtest showed this distance rule kept the plan out of several major moves; removing it added 4 trades and nearly doubled max profit.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = trend aligned (TS>KS, Chikou open space) AND price within gate distance of Kijun. Invalidation = price stays outside gate (no equalization) -> no trade; the rule is a filter, not a standalone signal. Warning in book: 'far' values vary with volatility, must be volatility-scaled.
risk_geometry: Entry only when within distance; stop = Kijun minus buffer; if entry risk exceeds cap, skip. This refines the existing trend_pullback family's entry condition (add a max-distance-from-baseline gate).
quote: When price is far away from the Kijun Sen it shows that price has moved at a faster rate than the Kijun Sen... there is a high probability that price will retract toward the Kijun Sen causing a major pullback or even a trend reversal.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 1 'Kijun Sen' (pp.14-17); entry-distance rules in Chapter 2 (p.43); optimization in Chapter 4 (p.141)
notes: The 1.5x ATR 'far' threshold is the falsifiable, volatility-scaled form and is directly usable in V8 with atr_ref. The fixed-pip thresholds do not transfer to BTC; scale by ATR or %. Refinement direction: trend_pullback variant gated on distance-to-Kijun, and a dead-thesis variant: far + flat Kijun = pullback risk.

strategy_name: Bull and bear traps
setup_summary: The index shows the book's consolidation chapter ends with 'Bull and Bear Traps' (pp.184-186): a false breakout of a range that traps breakout traders and then reverses. This is the classic failed-breakout/false-break mechanism: price pierces a range boundary, fails to follow through, and re-enters the range, squeezing the trapped side. Falsifiable: a candle closes beyond the range boundary and then closes back inside within N bars.

risk_geometry: Counter-entry at the close back through the boundary; stop beyond the trapped extreme (the false-break extreme); target back to the opposite range edge.

strategy_name: Potential Reversal Zone (PRZ) Fibonacci-convergence reversal
mechanism: 3+ independent Fibonacci projections/retracements of a 5-point structure converging in a narrow price zone mark a high-probability trend-change area
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, fit a 5-point XABCD swing structure and compute XA retracement at D, the BC projection (paired reciprocally to the C retracement), and the AB=CD completion. The PRZ is the band where >=3 of these levels converge tightly (book: within a few points/ticks on index charts; suggest <=1 ATR band on 1h perp). Enter in the zone on the initial test; a valid reversal requires the whole range to be tested and price to stabilize/reverse, not just touch the nearest number.
trigger_invalidation: The entire PRZ must be tested on the initial test and price must react; a price gap/displacement THROUGH the whole PRZ without any reaction (book: 'blowout') invalidates the setup; if price continues in the prior trend after the full test, the reversal thesis is dead.
risk_geometry: Entry is a zone/limit order around the pattern completion (book: 'executing in the zone'); stop = Stop Loss Zone (SLZ) just beyond the PRZ (for retracement patterns, violation of the X point itself is an explicit stop trigger); initial target = IPO at 0.382 or 0.618 retracement of the pattern range (A-to-D); expiry per the time projections (min 0.382 time, see time finding).
quote: Specific price structures that possess three or more numbers within a defined area are the basis for defining these harmonic zones.
chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'Potential Reversal Zone (PRZ)', pp. 39-40; Ch 9 execution pp. 174-176
notes: The definitive falsifiable core of the book: exact ratio alignments, no statistical support (chart examples only). On perps, 'gap through the PRZ' translates to a fast displacement/liquidation-cascade bar since 24/7 tape has no gaps. Book also notes larger price legs make more significant zones and psychological levels (50/100/1000) complement harmonic levels - both minor notes for the zone-significance feature.

strategy_name: AB=CD equidistant-leg pattern with reciprocal C-to-BC ratios
mechanism: after a leg AB and pullback to C, an equidistant CD leg completes at a predictable D where the BC projection converges with the C-point retracement via a fixed reciprocal-ratio table
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h, after swing AB, the C point must retrace AB by one of 0.382/0.50/0.618/0.707/0.786/0.886. The BC projection is the reciprocal of the C retracement (0.382->2.24/2.618; 0.50->2.0; 0.618->1.618; 0.707->1.41; 0.786->1.27; 0.886->1.13). The PRZ is where the projected D (CD length == AB length) converges with the BC projection; D completion is a mandatory requirement before entry. Alternate (1.27/1.618) AB=CD structures complement extension patterns.
trigger_invalidation: The AB=CD completion point is the mandatory trigger; a trade is invalid if CD diverges materially from the AB=CD completion area, or if the reciprocal BC projection fails to converge with it.
risk_geometry: Entry at/just beyond the AB=CD completion point; for retracement patterns the X point is the stop reference; initial targets are the 0.382/0.618 pattern-range retracements; no expiry stated other than time-symmetry preference (equivalent leg duration).
quote: a 0.618 retracement at the C point typically will possess a 1.618 BC projection that converges closest with the completion of the AB=CD
chapter_anchor: Ch 4 'The AB=CD Pattern', pp. 41-69
notes: Book warns 'the idea of trading every AB=CD that completes is absurd' - structure needs confirmation (other converging Fibonacci levels). Reciprocal-ratio table is a concrete, testable rule for the D-zone feature set.

strategy_name: Ideal Butterfly pattern - 0.786 B point with 1.27 XA projection
mechanism: a mandatory 0.786 B retracement sets up a milder 1.27 XA extension with a compact BC projection; strongest at all-time high/low territory where it can end the predominant trend
setup_summary: On BTCUSDT 1h: B at precise 0.786 of XA; D at the exclusive 1.27 XA projection (NO 1.618 XA projection); BC projection >=1.618 but compact (1.618/2.0/2.24 best; 2.618 sometimes); equivalent AB=CD minimum, Alternate 1.27 AB=CD most common and rarely exceeded; C retrace 0.382-0.886 (0.618 preferred). Book: 'The ideal Butterfly works well in new high/low territory' - valid patterns frequently end the predominant trend.
trigger_invalidation: A 1.618 XA projection means it is a Crab, not a Butterfly; BC projections should complete 'in a compact area' with the 1.27 XA; blowout of the PRZ invalidates.
risk_geometry: Entry at the 1.27 XA projection (defining limit of PRZ); tighter structure than Crab ('tame' BC projection); IPO 0.382/0.618 targets; X-point stop for retracement-class treatment applies to the retest-of-extreme nature of the pattern.
quote: a mandatory 0.786 retracement of the XA leg as the B point is the defining element of an ideal Butterfly pattern
chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'The Ideal Butterfly Pattern', pp. 149-169
notes: The book's exemplars are regime-end reversals (SPY 2009 low, Citigroup 2008 top). For BTCUSDT 1h, the 'new-high/low territory' context is common; the 0.786-B / 1.27-XA ratio pair is the falsifiable signature.

strategy_name: Failed-pattern continuation - reverse the trade on PRZ/T-bar violation
mechanism: when a reversal zone is blown out (gap/displacement or extreme expansion through the entire PRZ and T-bar), the failure signals overwhelming trend strength and the continuation of the predominant trend becomes the trade
setup_summary: After a harmonic reversal setup is entered and the T-bar extreme is violated (book: typically 1-2 bars beyond the T-bar, often confirmed by a gap/expansion close through the zone), cover/flip and trade continuation in the prior trend direction. Stop just beyond the violated zone (book example: prior week high for a failed bullish pattern; 'a simple 1-bar stop loss would have been more than adequate').
trigger_invalidation: Requires the entire PRZ to have been tested with only a nominal initial reaction first; the violation must be a clear, confirmed signal (convincing continuation after the T-bar break) - 'frequent stop-outs can occur before the price continues in the predominant trend'.
risk_geometry: Entry 1-2 bars beyond the T-bar; tight stop at the extreme of the violated PRZ / T-bar; stop then trails per subsequent bars (book: 'after confirming the violation, the stop loss is usually determined by the prior price bar(s) beyond the Terminal Price Bar'); targets not specified for the continuation leg.
quote: Because pattern failures are a sign of an overwhelming predominant trend, these technical events can serve as important continuation signals.
chapter_anchor: Ch 12 'Pattern Violations', pp. 233-250
notes: Direct refinement of the existing V8 failed_breakout expert (liquidity_vacuum_reentry, frozen prior_high_ref, SHORT): adds (a) both directions, (b) T-bar-based entry timing, (c) harmonic-zone context. Blowouts map naturally to perp liquidation cascades; tight stop discipline is mandatory.
book: Harmonic Trading, Volume One - Profiting from the Natural Order of the Financial Markets 2010

strategy_name: ABCD pullback continuation
setup_summary: On a 5m chart of a high-relative-volume instrument: a strong rally from A makes a new session high at B; price pulls back to C which holds above the A origin (a higher low) for at least one consolidation period; enter long near C-close, stop below C, target the D extension (new high). Never chase at B.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = C holds as support (buyers defend C). Invalidation = close below point C; also do not enter if pullback has no definable floor (stop cannot be placed).
risk_geometry: Entry near C (bar close); stop below C (structure, not a fixed ATR multiple); target D (structure/new high); sell half at D and move stop to break-even; remainder exits on target, on 5m new-low weakness signal, or when buyers exhaust.
quote: If the price moves higher, I sell half of my position at point D, and bring my stop higher to my entry point (break-even).
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 1 (ABCD Pattern), lines 1163-1192
notes: Directly corroborates the existing trend_pullback expert family (ema_fast>ema_slow, close<ema_slow): ABCD replaces the EMA filter with a structural higher-low (C above A). Refinement input: frozen C-support ref, half-out-at-D break-even, still_valid = price holds above C. Book's self-fulfilling-prophecy rationale (many traders watch the same level) is the stated edge mechanism.
book: How to Day Trade for a Living - Tools, Tactics, Money Management, Discipline and Trading Psychology 3rd edition

strategy_name: Moving Average trend ride (9 EMA as moving support/resistance)
setup_summary: After the high-volatility session open, a trend establishes around the 9 EMA on 1m/5m charts; enter long on a pullback to the 9 EMA that holds as support (short below it when it holds as resistance), buying as close to the MA as possible; ride until a 5m candle closes through the MA.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = EMA holds as support/resistance with price respecting it. Invalidation = 5m candle CLOSE through the EMA (wick breaks with low volume are false breakouts and do not stop the thesis); for shorts a close above the MA.
risk_geometry: Entry at/near MA; stop 5-10 cents below MA or on 5m candle close below MA; no fixed R target — exit on MA break; optional half-profit at extended moves (no trailing stops; manual monitoring).
quote: My stop will usually be 5 to 10 cents below the moving average line or, if a candlestick, close below the moving average (for long positions).
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 5 (Moving Average Trend Trading), lines 1345-1387
notes: Refinement input for trend_pullback: (1) close-based (not wick-based) EMA break as the still_valid termination — this is exactly the close-through-EMA exit discipline V8's NEXT_BAR_CLOSE semantics can express; (2) low-volume false-breakout filter (a wick through the EMA on low relative volume is not a thesis kill). Book notes trend trades hold hours and work best mid-session, i.e., a time-of-day regime dependency.

strategy_name: Bull Flag momentum breakout with volume confirmation
setup_summary: On a short timeframe (1m-5m): a vertical pole of large up-candles is followed by a sideways consolidation of small candles; enter when price moves over the high of the consolidation candlesticks, with share volume significantly higher after consolidation as confirmation; stop below the consolidation low. Trade only the first and second consolidation periods of a run.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = close above the consolidation high with volume expansion. Invalidation = close below the consolidation low (breakdown); third-and-higher consolidation periods are not traded (buyers likely losing control).
risk_geometry: Entry on consolidation-breakout (scalp style); stop = breakdown of consolidation; target = next resistance / profit target, book recommends quick scalp for low-float under-$10; exit half, move to break-even, remainder on loss of steam (new 5m low).
quote: As soon as prices are moving over the high of the consolidation candlesticks, I enter the trade. My stop loss is the break below the consolidation periods.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 2 (Bull Flag Momentum), lines 1196-1238
notes: Low-float-stock manipulation dynamics do not map to BTCUSDT 1h, but the pole-consolidation-breakout-with-volume-confirmation pattern is transferable to high-relative-volume episodes. Book flags this as the riskiest strategy requiring fast execution and scalping exits — the canonical L1 fill-at-close simulator can express it only coarsely, hence BACKLOG_CANDIDATE rather than PROPOSE_NEW_EXPERT.

strategy_name: Opening Range Breakout (5/15/30 min)
setup_summary: Define the first 5m (or 15m/30m) candle range at session open; REQUIRE the range width to be significantly smaller than the daily ATR (else the stock is too volatile to give a catchable directional move); enter in the breakout direction when price breaks the range high (long) or low (short); stop = close back through VWAP (close below VWAP for longs, break above for shorts); target = next technical level, daily MA, or previous day close.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = close outside the opening range in a clear direction. Invalidation = close back inside the range or through VWAP; if the opening range is near/above daily ATR, do not trade (no directional signal).
risk_geometry: Entry on range-break; stop = close through VWAP; target = next technical level (intraday level, daily MA, PDC); if no level, exit on weakness (new 5m low for longs) / strength (new 5m high for shorts).
quote: The opening range must be significantly smaller than the stock's Average True Range (ATR).
chapter_anchor: Ch 7, Strategy 9 (Opening Range Breakouts), lines 1520-1559
notes: Equities version relies on the 9:30 opening auction and overnight-gap psychology that crypto lacks, but a session-open range is definable (e.g., first N bars of the UTC day or after a funding-settlement window). The range-width-vs-ATR filter is a falsifiable, high-value addition to any breakout family. ORB is described as an entry signal only — target and stop must come from other levels, so it is a candidate behavior family more than a standalone edge.

strategy_name: Gartley 222 retest entry
mechanism: a four-leg X-A-B-C-D structure containing a valid AB=CD retests a prior extreme and offers a low-risk trend-direction entry before the bigger move
setup_summary: X is the anchor (recent swing high/low, possibly on a higher timeframe). Leg XA forms, AB retraces to a Fibonacci level, the embedded AB=CD completes at D. Primary D completion is at .786 of XA (also .618/.50/.382; .382 in strong trends). Buy a higher low / sell a lower high - a retest entry into the established trend. Invalidations: D cannot exceed X; C cannot exceed A; B cannot exceed X (then it becomes a Butterfly).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price reaches D at the .786 retracement of XA with the internal AB=CD valid. Invalidated: D exceeds X, C exceeds A, or B exceeds X; wide-range bar or gap at D (warning sign) -> wait for confirmation.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit just beyond D (.786). Stop: beyond X (1.00) if risk acceptable, else fixed dollar amount (e.g., 8 cents/soybeans, $5.50/GOOG). Target 1 = amount risked (breakeven stop after), target 2 = .618 of AD. Trailing: stop below the .786 of the most recent retracement after price makes .382 off AD. 2-3 part scale-outs.
quote: By definition, it is buying a higher low or selling a lower high, which is ideal for trading with the trend.
chapter_anchor: Ch 5, Trading the Gartley "222" Pattern
notes: Trend-following retest with limit entry and quantified risk - well suited to 24/7 perps where retests of swing extremes are frequent and limit fills are reliable. Distinct from existing EMA-based trend_pullback (different trigger: harmonic swing completion vs EMA cross). Gartley's 'profitable in 7 out of 10 cases over 30 years' is an assertion, not a presented study.
book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

strategy_name: Fibonacci retracement entry in an established trend
mechanism: in a trend, pullbacks find support/resistance at Fibonacci retracement levels of the prior impulse leg, so entering at .382-.786 of XA is a trend-continuation entry
setup_summary: Two legs only (XA impulse, AB retracement) - no AB=CD required. In an established trend, enter with a limit at the .382/.50/.618/.786 retracement of XA, in the trend direction. Strongest trends retrace only .382/.50; bar-count symmetry between XA and AB (equal bars or Fibonacci ratio of bar counts) adds confluence. Rapid 2-3 bar AB completion is a warning sign to wait.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price trades into the Fib retracement zone of XA in a trend. Invalidated/stand-aside: long wide-range bar just before the level (wait for .786 or momentum slowdown); AB completes in far fewer bars than XA; deep retracement beyond 1.00.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit at Fib level. Stop: just beyond X (1.00) or beyond swing low/high. Target 1 = amount risked (e.g., $1.45 INTC), then opposite Fib levels or the D of a forming AB=CD. Refines V8 trend_pullback: replaces EMA-cross trigger with swing-based Fib retracement level + bar-count confluence.
quote: A retracement-type pattern gives the trader an advantage of not having to try to pick a top or a bottom - it is an entry into a trade in the direction of the trend.
chapter_anchor: Ch 8, Fibonacci Retracement Pattern Structure
notes: Directly testable on BTCUSDT 1h (swing detection + retracement levels + bar-count symmetry). Closely related to existing trend_pullback; a shallow-retracement variant (.382/.50 in strong trends) with Fib-level entry is a natural family variant, keeping the one-family-one-unit multiplicity rule.
book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

strategy_name: NR7 trend-day regime filter with shallow-pullback entries
mechanism: volatility contraction (NR7) precedes expansion; trend days open near one extreme, hold gaps, and produce shallow repetitive corrections, so pullback entries have tight quantifiable stops
setup_summary: Regime filter: NR7 (narrowest range of the past 7 sessions) precedes trend days; confirmation of a trend day = open at/near one extreme, gap held with no fill attempt, wide range bars in the first 15-30 minutes, neutral closes. On a confirmed trend day: enter shallow pullbacks/consolidations (corrections 1.25-3.5 points, rarely beyond 5.5 points; .382/.50 retracements using the opening price) in the trend direction. Trend is over when new highs stop being made or support breaks.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: trend-day conditions confirmed; enter on the next 2-3 point pullback or consolidation. Invalidated: correction exceeds the 5.5-point pullback rule; failure to make a new high after a pullback (trend over). Countertrend entries on a trend day are the book's primary warning.
risk_geometry: Entry: limit 2 points into a shallow pullback / just above a consolidation level. Stop: 3 points initial, placed below the wide-range-bar low or below the trend pullback level; trail above/below last small swing. Targets: retest of last high, then hold core into the close; add on subsequent patterns. Scale out into the close.
quote: A narrowing of range, referred to as an NR7, which is defined as the narrowest range in the past seven trading days.
chapter_anchor: Ch 10, Identifying a Trend Day
notes: NR7 and shallow-repetitive-correction behavior are measurable on 24/7 crypto (UTC-day candles replace the session; 'gap held' becomes 'opening range held'). Directly usable as a regime filter + variant of trend_pullback (shallow .382/.50 pullback entry, tight stop). Book cites Crabel and Raschke statistical research without reproducing it.
book: Trade What You See - How To Profit from Pattern Recognition 2007

strategy_name: Warning-sign/confirmation-bar entry filter
mechanism: momentum overshoot at pattern completion: wide-range bars, gaps, tail closes, and steep final legs indicate price will exceed the completion point, so delaying entry one time bar filters the overshoot
setup_summary: Methodology applied to all pattern completions (AB=CD, Gartley, etc.). Warning signs (gap in the CD leg, wide range bar ~2x normal at/near completion, tail closes, very steep CD vs AB) -> pass or wait. Confirmation signs (tweezer top/bottom, gap in the trade direction, close at range extreme in trade direction, or waiting one full time bar after the trigger) -> low-risk entry with a stop under the confirmation bar.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - this is an entry-timing filter on pattern completions, not a standalone setup. Both branches (warning -> stand aside; confirmation -> enter next bar) are implementable as a variant of any pattern expert.
risk_geometry: Entry: NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after trigger (matching V8 simulator convention) or after a confirmation bar; stop just below the tweezer/confirmation low. Waiting one bar is the core rule: 'daily time frame waits one daily bar, 5-minute time frame waits one 5-minute bar'.
quote: Waiting one time bar can be used when the trader has reason to believe, based on price behavior, that price may exceed the completion point of a pattern.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11, Warning Signs and Confirmation Signs
notes: Feeds bar-range, tail (close vs high/low position), and wick features into marketstate; 'wait one bar' is a cheap entry-delay variant in the simulator. The overshoot claim (price exceeds D when momentum is extreme) is a falsifiable feature test across all pattern experts.

strategy_name: Harmonic-number swing-amplitude stop placement
mechanism: each market has a reproducible dominant swing amplitude ('harmonic number'); the dominant swing size on the traded timeframe is the natural stop distance and pullback target
setup_summary: Empirical methodology: measure the most common recurring swing amplitude on the traded timeframe (e.g., S&P 5.4 pts, euro 70 pips, gold 11/17, crude 44/88) from a sample (book suggests ~100 swings); use it as the stop distance (or 3% of instrument price as a proxy harmonic, e.g., IBM $99.48 -> $2.98 harmonic used as a stop) and as a pullback target. Harmonics on smaller timeframes relate to larger ones by 1/2 or .618. Expansions (2x-3x the harmonic) signal trend mode.
trigger_invalidation: N/A - a stop/target calibration methodology applied within pattern experts.
risk_geometry: Stop distance = dominant harmonic swing amplitude (or 3%-of-price proxy) placed beyond the swing high/low; profit target = harmonic projection down/up from the extreme; replaces a universal ATR multiple with an instrument-specific amplitude calibrated per timeframe.
quote: The 3 percent harmonic would be approximately $2.98... We can use $2.98 for placing a stop-loss order if buying the pullback.
chapter_anchor: Ch 3, Using the 3 Percent Rule for Finding a Harmonic Number
notes: The usable core for V8 is 'dominant swing amplitude per timeframe as stop distance', which is testable as a robust percentile of swing ranges on BTCUSDT 1h. The fixed 3%-of-price variant transfers poorly to crypto (regime-varying volatility), and the harmonic-number mysticism (Gann/astrology lineage) is not evidence. More natural as a stop-calibration input to atr_stop than as a standalone strategy.

strategy_name: New-high pullback short (stop-cluster retracement)
mechanism: protective stop-loss orders clustered just beyond prior highs get absorbed by the breakout, then sellers exceed buyers and price pulls back after every new high is scored
setup_summary: After price takes out a significant prior high (book example: a multi-month GBP high), switch to a 15-min chart and short on the bar close of a bearish candlestick formation (evening star, bearish engulfing, tweezer top); book cites a 200-pip drop in ~45 minutes. Mirror going long at new lows with bullish formations.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid if price keeps making new highs after entry (bulls keep scoring points / channel shifts up): 'If the bulls take out the high, they will more than likely keep on going.'
risk_geometry: Entry: next bar close after a bearish candle at/just after the new high. Stop: a little beyond the last high of resistance (last low for longs). Target: first pullback support — past support, uptrend line, or Fibonacci retracement; no explicit R-multiple or expiry stated.
quote: most of the time, after the bulls achieve a new high, frequently prices start to retrace, or fall back down
chapter_anchor: Ch 5 'Resistance and Support' / 'How Do Bulls and Bears Score Points?' (pp.73-81)
notes: The book explicitly roots the pullback in stop-order clusters near last highs — a liquidity mechanism, not just mean reversion. In crypto perps, leverage + 24/7 trading concentrate stops at prior highs/round levels; testable as a location+response family. Distinct from V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim (no wick-through-close sweep required; entry is the rejection candle after a clean new high).

strategy_name: Trend-line cascade bounce (inner -> outer -> long-term)
mechanism: correctly drawn trend lines act as floors/ceilings; the market bounces off each line in the trend direction and only a full cascade of breaks signals major reversal
setup_summary: In an uptrend, buy the bounce when price retraces to the inner or outer uptrend line (lines drawn across wick lows; outer at ~45 degrees) while price remains above the outer line ('80 percent chance' of continuation, asserted). If the inner line breaks, expect price to travel to the outer line and bounce there; if the outer breaks, to the long-term line; a long-term line break implies major reversal. Mirror for downtrends.
trigger_invalidation: Thesis invalid on a decisive close beyond the respective trend line; long-term line break = major reversal, do not re-enter.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at/after the trend-line touch. Stop: just beyond the trend line (below it for longs). Target: next higher trend line / prior high; no explicit R-multiple or expiry. Book's probability claims (80% continuation) are asserted, not measured.
quote: If the inner trend line is broken, the market usually moves to the outer trend line and will bounce back up from there... If the long-term trend line is broken, as a rule there will be a major reversal.
chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Finding and Drawing Inner, Outer, and Long-term Uptrend Lines' (pp.96-104); Ch 6 'The Value of Trend Lines' (pp.111)
notes: Distinct from the existing trend_pullback family (EMA-based): this is a geometric trend-line family. Falsifiability requires a deterministic line-fitting rule (regression across wick lows/highs), which the book only describes qualitatively — formalize before coding. The 80% figure is practitioner assertion.

strategy_name: Zone-break angle filter (buy/sell zone entry)
mechanism: after a trend line is broken, the position of the line's extension ('backside') relative to the last swing extreme determines whether the break is a true reversal or a channel shift
setup_summary: When price closes through an uptrend line into the sell zone, compare the trend-line extension to the last swing high: if the backside of the line is lower than the last high, short with a claimed 80% probability of continued dip/reversal; if higher than the last high, expect continued rally (channel shift). Mirror for downtrend lines entering the buy zone. Require the breaking candle itself to be a bearish (or bullish) decision candle — a counter-candle at the break means the trend is still intact.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if a bullish candle appears immediately at the break of an uptrend line (market 'still potentially bullish'), or if price reclaims the last high.
risk_geometry: Entry: after bar close into the zone (next bar). Stop: 'above the last high of resistance' for shorts / below last low for longs. Target: next support/resistance; no explicit R-multiple or expiry.
quote: If the backside of the trend line is lower than the last high, there is an 80 percent chance of a continued dip and a trend reversal. If the backside of the trend line is higher than the last high, there is an 80 percent chance of a continued rally.
chapter_anchor: Ch 7 'The Sell Zone' and 'The Buy Zone' (pp.117-125)
notes: Gated on subjective line placement + angle measurement; needs a precise line-fitting spec to be falsifiable, hence backlog not formalize. Crypto: bar-close zone breaks are clean (no exchange gaps), but BTC trend lines are noisy vs FX 45-degree norms.

strategy_name: Consolidation range fade with candlestick confirmation
mechanism: inside a sideways range, institutional sellers at resistance and buyers at support push price back to the opposite side of the range; a missing reversal candle at the boundary is itself a signal of imminent breakout
setup_summary: Identify a consolidation (equal highs/lows; book: ranges ~150-300 pips on larger TFs, market is sideways 50-60% of the time). Sell at resistance on the close of a bearish candlestick formation; buy at support on a bullish formation; ride to the opposite side of the range and repeat until breakout. If no candlestick formation appears near a boundary, the market is likely about to break out — stand aside.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if price closes beyond the range boundary (by construction no reversal candle formed) or the range expands.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close of reversal candle at the range boundary. Stop: beyond the range boundary (past resistance for shorts, past support for longs). Target: the opposite side of the range; no explicit R-multiple or expiry.
quote: you need to sell at the level of resistance and buy at a level of support when you find a consolidation in the market.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'Strategy 1' (pp.178-181); Ch 3 sideways-market discussion (p.40)
notes: Book insists trend systems bleed out in sideways markets and a trader needs BOTH a trend system and a range system — a direct argument for a range_reversion family in V8's portfolio (complexity budget still gates to 3 active). Crypto ranges frequently; equal-high/low detection is mechanical.
book: The 10 Essentials of Forex Trading - The Rules for Turning Trading Patterns Into Profit 2007

strategy_name: Pre-announcement consolidation straddle breakout
mechanism: immediately before a scheduled macro announcement traders stand aside, compressing price into a tight range; the release triggers a directional breakout whose expected magnitude scales with range duration
setup_summary: Five minutes before a scheduled fundamental announcement, with price in a 20-60 pip tight range, place a buy stop 15 pips above resistance and a sell stop 10 pips below support (spread-adjusted: +5 pips); the longer the pre-announcement range, the more aggressive the expected breakout. If a triggered order is stopped out and price returns into the range, the book says the market tends to then go the other way — keep the second order live.
trigger_invalidation: If the market returns into the range after triggering one side, favor the opposite direction; on a no-change announcement expect continuation of the prior trend rather than a breakout.
risk_geometry: Entry: resting stop orders (buy 15 pips above resistance, sell 10 pips below support). Stops: sell stop 15 pips above last high, buy stop 10 pips below last low. Target: next past support/resistance levels; book warns of 30-100 pip slippage on fills and 200-pip/20-second spikes.
quote: Place a buy order 15 pips above or north of the resistance level and 10 pips below or south of the level of support, or the trading range.
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'Strategy 2' (pp.181-183); Ch 10 'Trading Days versus Trending Days' (pp.167-170)
notes: The book notes brokers largely eliminated straddling because of slippage — the same failure mode applies to fast crypto macro candles (CPI/FOMC/NFP) and liquidation cascades. The spread-adjusted stop math is venue-specific (Binance USDM taker fees differ from FX pip spreads). Needs the crypto macro-calendar feature before it is testable.

strategy_name: Bull/bear trap fade (false breakout of consolidation)
mechanism: with no scheduled catalyst, a breakout out of consolidation is a false move ('fulfilling the natural numerical sequence') and price U-turns back in the direction of the prior trend toward the D extension
setup_summary: After a consolidation with no scheduled fundamental announcement, a breakout to the south (bull trap) or north (bear trap) that fails and closes back inside the range signals reversal back toward the prior trend; enter on the return close in the prior-trend direction.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the breakout continues beyond the fake-out extreme (genuine breakout), or if an unscheduled catalyst/announcement appears.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close back inside the range after the false breakout. Stop: beyond the fake-out extreme. Target: direction of the prior trend toward the Fibonacci D extension; no explicit R-multiple or expiry.
quote: bull traps are false breakouts to the south out of that consolidation, doing nothing more than fulfilling the natural numerical sequence of the market, then U-turning back in the direction of the previous trend
chapter_anchor: Ch 11 'Bull and Bear Traps' (pp.184-185)
notes: Conceptually adjacent to V8's failed_breakout (liquidity_vacuum_reentry) but contextually distinct — it happens at a consolidation boundary rather than a prior high, and its precondition is 'no scheduled announcement'. Best handled as a variant of the failed_breakout family (one multiplicity unit). The 'no announcement' precondition maps to the crypto macro calendar + funding/expiry windows.

strategy_name: Trend-filtered candlestick reversal patterns
mechanism: reversal candlestick formations (morning star, bullish engulfing, tweezer bottom / evening star, bearish engulfing, tweezer top) signal U-turns only when they appear in the direction of the prevailing trend and only after the final candle closes with confirmation
setup_summary: In an uptrend (candles above the outer uptrend line) buy only bullish formations: morning star (large bearish decision candle -> 1-4 indecision candles -> bullish close beyond the 60% mark of the first candle), bullish engulfing (opens below prior close and engulfs 1-3 prior candles), or tweezer bottom (two+ indecision candles with long lower wicks at near-equal lows, forming support). Mirror the three bearish formations in a downtrend. Ignore all formations inside a 20-40 pip (ATR-scaled for crypto) sideways range.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the confirming candle fails to close beyond the 60% mark of the first candle, or the pattern forms in a flat/consolidating range (book: these 'should be ignored').
risk_geometry: Entry: only after the last candle of the formation closes ('wait until the last candle closes before you enter the market'). Stop: protective stop beyond the pattern extreme / last support. Target: not explicitly defined beyond trend continuation.
quote: in a downtrend, only trade bearish candlestick formations, not bullish... In trading any candlestick formation, you must wait until the last candle closes before you enter the market
chapter_anchor: Ch 4 'Bullish/Bearish Candlestick Formations' and 'Trading Candlestick Patterns' (pp.57-69)
notes: The tweezer bottom/top is a double-test of support/resistance — related to V8 liquidity_sweep_reclaim but without the wick-through-close sweep. The candle-close rule matches V8's NEXT_BAR_CLOSE convention. Requires a 'response' feature (candle body/wick geometry) plus the trend filter; the 20-40 pip exclusion must be ATR-scaled for BTCUSDT.

strategy_name: Trading-day vs trending-day regime filter
mechanism: on days with scheduled macro announcements the market consolidates before the release, then trends 120-240 pips in the first hours; on quiet days it drifts only 60-90 pips, and a consolidation with no catalyst is thin late-session drift
setup_summary: Classify sessions by scheduled macro releases: announcement days => pre-release consolidation then a 120-240-pip directional move in the first five hours (trending day); no-announcement days => 60-90 pip drift (trading day). Novices should avoid entering in the announcement window (30-100 pip slippage, 200-pip/20-second spikes); a consolidation with no announcement scheduled should be traded in the direction of the prior trend.
trigger_invalidation: Regime filter, not a trade thesis: the classification flips on the economic calendar; unscheduled events (assassination attempts, surprise rate changes, 9/11-type shocks) can override the calendar.
risk_geometry: n/a — regime/risk filter; the book recommends standing aside during the announcement window and warns of extreme slippage and whipsaws (Ch 10 figures 10-4, 10-5).
quote: Trading days are when there are no fundamental announcements. Currency charts move typically 60 to 90 pips... Trending days are fundamental announcement days, when the market will generally take off in a direction after the announcement and move 120 to 240 pips within the first five hours.
chapter_anchor: Ch 10 'Trading Days versus Trending Days' (pp.167-170); Ch 11 'Strategy 3' (pp.183)
notes: Do not default to HIGH: FX announcement behavior (interest-rate/employment releases) is not identical to crypto macro moves, but FOMC/CPI/NFP demonstrably move BTC. Implementable as a MarketState feature flag 'scheduled_macro_event' + consolidation state; also relevant to funding-rate settlement windows.

strategy_name: Higher-timeframe trend controls lower-timeframe entries
mechanism: moves on lower timeframes are corrections of higher-timeframe moves, so a signal taken off a single timeframe often lands at the end of that timeframe's trend right when the higher timeframe reverses
setup_summary: Before trading a lower timeframe, establish the higher-timeframe regime: a 200-pip retracement on the daily chart is a complete downtrend on the 60-minute chart, so a 60-min-only bias enters at the end of the move just as the daily hits its trend line and reverses. Use the larger timeframe's trend line/regime as the admission filter for lower-timeframe signals, and check that smaller-TF candles are on the correct side of the larger-TF trend line.
trigger_invalidation: n/a — methodology rule governing signal admissibility, not a trade thesis.
risk_geometry: n/a — methodology; the book's corollary is that trend systems lose money in sideways regimes (market consolidates 50-60% of the time), so a two-system split (trend + range) is needed.
quote: the movement on smaller time frames will always respond to the trend lines on larger time frames.
chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Finding and Drawing Inner, Outer, and Long-term Uptrend Lines' (pp.100-101); Ch 3 'Using Multiple Time Frames to Trade' (pp.44)
notes: Direct architectural input: each V8 Expert's MarketState should include the higher-timeframe trend/regime as context (e.g., 4h trend line side as a filter for 1h signals) rather than each Expert re-deriving regime from a single TF. Also grounds the book's claim that trend-following systems need a separate range system.

strategy_name: Inside Day Breakout (volatility compression expansion)
mechanism: Two or more inside days compress the daily range; expansion releases the compression, and the breakout direction can be biased by the contraction's location within a triangle or by momentum.
setup_summary: On the daily chart, identify at least two consecutive inside days (each day's high/low contained within the prior day's range). Place a buy stop 10 pips above the prior inside day's high and a sell stop 10 pips below its low; stop-and-reverse 10 pips beyond the inside-day extreme. Target 2R or trail. Bias direction with formation geometry (ascending-triangle contraction near range top favors upside) and MACD histogram sign.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: break of prior inside-day high/low by 10 pips. Invalidation: stop-and-reverse triggered (first move was a false breakout) - thesis flips to the opposite direction.
risk_geometry: Entry: 10 pips beyond inside-day high/low (daily bars); stop-and-reverse 10 pips past the inside-day low/high; target 2R or trailing stop; daily-bar expiry.
quote: There need to be at least two inside days before the volatility play can be implemented. The more inside days, the higher the likelihood of an upside surge.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Inside Day Breakout Play', p. 88-92
notes: Cleanly portable to perps: no overnight/exchange gaps, so inside-day containment is well-defined; compression-to-expansion is frequent in BTC. The both-sided stop-and-reverse structure maps naturally to a V8 candidate hypothesis in the breakout family.

strategy_name: Filtering False Breakouts (20-day high shakeout re-break)
mechanism: A 20-day high followed by a fast flush to a 2-day low shakes out weak longs; re-break of the 20-day high confirms real-money re-entry and strong trend continuation.
setup_summary: Daily bars: pair makes a new 20-day high (or 20-day low for the short side); within the next 3 days it reverses to a 2-day low (or 2-day high); buy if it takes out the 20-day high within 3 days of the 2-day low. Stop a few pips below the 2-day low; target 2R or trail (two-bar low).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: 20-day extreme made, then a 2-day counter-extreme within 3 days, then re-break within 3 days. Invalidation: stop below the 2-day counter-extreme; no re-break within the 3-day window.
risk_geometry: Entry: re-break of the 20-day extreme; stop a few pips beyond the 2-day counter-extreme; target 2R or trailing stop.
quote: Look for a currency pair that is making a 20-day high. Look for the pair to reverse over the next three days to make a two-day low. Buy the pair if it takes out the 20-day high within three days of making the two-day low.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Filtering False Breakouts', p. 94-96
notes: Distinct from failed_breakout (which trades the reversal) and from a plain pullback-to-support: this is a continuation entry after a shallow flush in a strong trend. Well-defined, fully falsifiable time windows (3-day / 2-day / 20-day) make it a strong backlog candidate.

strategy_name: Perfect Order (stacked MA trend regime)
mechanism: Sequential stacking of 10/20/50/100/200-day SMAs aligns momentum with the trend direction and marks a persistent trending regime (momentum alignment = trend persistence).
setup_summary: Uptrend: 10>20>50>100>200-day SMA stacked in descending order (mirror for short). Treat perfect order as a trend-state condition: enter when the stack first forms (book's examples enter ~5 bars later), stay long while it holds, exit when the order breaks (20-day SMA crosses below the 10-day SMA); require ADX >20 and rising for confirmation.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: full MA stack in order with ADX rising. Invalidation: stack order broken (e.g., 20-day SMA below 10-day SMA).
risk_geometry: No fixed stop/target in the book; position held while the perfect order persists, exit on order break. Book examples: +410 pips risking 97 pips (long), +443 pips risking 149 pips (short).
quote: A perfect order is when the moving averages line up perfectly; that is for an uptrend, the 10-day SMA is greater than the 20-day SMA, which is greater than the 50-day SMA.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 8, 'Perfect Order', p. 97-98 (mechanism defined in Ch. 7 trend profiling, p. 70)
notes: Best used as a trend-state feature / regime gate for the trend_pullback family (only take pullbacks while the stack is in perfect order) rather than a standalone entry. ADX >20 rising confirmation per the book.

strategy_name: Option Volatility Term-Structure Timing (short vs long vol)
mechanism: When short-term (1M) volatility is well below long-term (3M) volatility, compression precedes a breakout; when short-term volatility is well above long-term volatility, expect reversion to a trading range.
setup_summary: Compute the spread between short-term (one-month) and long-term (three-month) volatility. If short << long, expect an imminent breakout (direction undefined) - favor breakout-family setups and tighten range-trade exits; if short >> long, expect reversion to range - favor mean-reversion entries. Book uses 1M vs 3M option volatilities; a realized-vol term structure is the tape-computable proxy.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: ST/LT vol divergence beyond normal. Invalidation: vol gap returns to neutral, or a suspected breakout fires against an open range position - book rule: if the break is likely against you, close the range trade.
risk_geometry: No entry geometry; it is a regime gate that also tells range traders when to exit (close range positions when short-term vol falls well below long-term vol).
quote: if short-term option volatilities are significantly lower than long-term volatilities, one should expect a breakout, though the direction of the breakout is not defined by this rule.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 9, 'Using Option Volatilities to Time Market Movements', p. 114-117 (also Ch. 7, p. 68-70)
notes: Directly implementable with realized-volatility term structure on the current tape; implied vol (Deribit) would be an options-data feature. This is a falsifiable regime gate that selects between breakout and mean-reversion behavior families.

strategy_name: Retail speculative flow contrarian (FXCM SSI)
mechanism: The retail crowd extrapolates the trend and is systematically wrong at turns; aggregate retail long/short positioning moves inversely to price, and the flip of the ratio (not the extreme) is the most accurate turn signal
setup_summary: Track the aggregate retail long/short ratio (% of open orders long). More than 50% long favors weakness, less than 50% long favors strength; SSI moves inversely to price. The flipping of the ratio is a more accurate turn signal than extreme positioning. A big fall in net positioning while price rises is bearish because short-covering is fueling the rally and price will decline when covering ends.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger on a flip in retail positioning near a multiweek extreme or on rising price with falling net positioning. Invalidated if retail positioning continues to extrapolate and price keeps trending (crowd can remain wrong for extended periods).
risk_geometry: None stated in book; indicator is a filter/overlay, not an entry.
quote: The SSI works as a contrarian indicator during trending markets. The flipping of the ratio is a more accurate signal of a turn in prices than extreme positioning.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 5, Other Sentiment Indicators — FXCM Speculative Sentiment Index, pp. 94-97
notes: Crypto analog: exchange-published long/short ratios, taker buy/sell flow, and funding rate. The 'rising price + falling net positioning = short-covering rally' claim is directly testable on perp OI/funding data. Evidence is interpretive guidance on a proprietary indicator (no public statistics).

strategy_name: Extreme-language news headline and magazine-cover contrarian
mechanism: Media only grants extreme coverage (headlines with surge/plummet/plunge/crash, cover stories, directional predictions) when the crowd is at a sentiment extreme; the media extrapolates the trend and is therefore wrong at the turn
setup_summary: When headlines about an asset use extreme language or take a directional stand (e.g., 'Dollar Surges...', 'Euroshambles', 'The Disappearing Dollar'), expect a short-term reversal over days-to-weeks (short-term) or weeks-to-months (magazine covers). Mundane headlines ('Euro rallies against Dollar') signal trend continuation. Google Trends news-reference volume spikes coincide with major turns ('weak dollar' search peaked at DXY bottoms in Dec 2004 and Nov 2006).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger on an extreme-language headline or directional media prediction for the traded asset. Invalidated if the trend continues — many headline examples preceded further trend (e.g., 'At Last, the Euro Looks Ready to Climb' preceded a further 14-month euro decline), so the signal is a warning, not a guarantee.
risk_geometry: Book calls it 'a risky trade outright' — no clean stop placement at multiweek/month/year extremes; use wave principle structure or pivot points for timing; can also be used as an exit overlay on existing positions.
quote: headlines that contain strong language and/or that take a directional stand are fantastic contrarian signals
chapter_anchor: Ch. 4, Using News Headlines to Generate Signals, pp. 53-68; Ch. 3, The Power of Magazine Covers, pp. 31-51
notes: Book cites a peer-reviewed study (Arnold, Earl & North, FAJ 2007) of 2,080 Business Week/Fortune/Forbes cover stories (1982-2002): cover stories follow extreme performance and signal its end. Crypto analog: mainstream Bitcoin 'crash'/hype coverage and search-volume spikes. Needs an external news/search-volume corpus not present in the perp tape.

strategy_name: Overbought/oversold as trend-continuation bias (anti-reversal RSI)
mechanism: Strong trends remain overbought/oversold for extended periods; an oscillator cross into extreme territory marks the start or middle of a trend, not its end — the bias flips only on an opposite-side cross
setup_summary: Maintain a bullish bias while weekly RSI has crossed above 60 (or 70) and has not yet crossed below 40 (or 30); bearish while crossed below 40 (or 30) without crossing above 60 (or 70). Repeated overshoots do not flip the bias. In the book's EURUSD weekly equity-curve tests (2001-2007), the trending interpretation of RSI 70/30, RSI 60/40, slow stochastics 80/20 and 70/30, and Bollinger 1/2-stdev all beat the corresponding reversal interpretations; the book's EURUSD weekly examples show RSI>70 marked the start of bull phases (Jun 2002, May 2006) and RSI<30 the start of bear phases.
trigger_invalidation: Bias flips only when the oscillator crosses the opposite threshold (bullish bias ends only on a cross below 40/30). Trading reversal on overbought/oversold is explicitly refuted by the equity-curve comparisons.
risk_geometry: Trend tests: stop-buy at the bar high when the bias flips long, stop-sell at the bar low when short. For entry refinement while bias is bullish: 'buy intra-week weakness by placing orders near the calculated weekly pivot supports'.
quote: RSI moving above 70 was much closer to the beginning of a bull trend than to the end. Similarly, RSI moving below 30 was much closer to the beginning of a bear trend than to the end.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Fancy Momentum Indicators and Overbought/Oversold, pp. 125-141
notes: Directly refutes the naive rsi_oversold_reversal usage. In V8 this is a regime filter that keeps trend-following experts (trend_pullback) engaged while oscillators are extreme, and a candidate refinement: overbought is confirmation of trend, not a fade signal.

strategy_name: Divergence and momentum-extreme caveats (methodology warning)
mechanism: Momentum (rate of change) peaks at the beginning or middle of a trend, not its end; divergence is present at every turn but does not always lead to a turn; arithmetic momentum distorts at tops/bottoms versus geometric rate of change
setup_summary: Use rate-of-change (geometric, log-scale) rather than arithmetic momentum for divergence: at the Dec 2004 EURUSD top, ROC identified bearish divergence while arithmetic momentum did not. Trade in the direction of a momentum extreme (ROC greatest over lookback), which marks the start/middle of a move (July 2002 EURUSD momentum extreme was mid-trend). A valid reversal fade requires a momentum extreme in the direction OPPOSITE the prior trend (USDCAD Nov 23 2007 bullish extreme after a downtrend).
trigger_invalidation: Do not treat divergence as a standalone reversal signal — divergence persisted through EURUSD 2002-2004 with only pauses/corrections; a divergence-based reversal entered early loses. Only momentum extremes opposite the prior trend direction are valid reversal candidates.
risk_geometry: None stated; bias-definition tool.
quote: Divergence is present at every turn, but divergence does not always lead to a turn.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Divergence and Using Momentum Extremes to Trade a Reversal, pp. 121-125
notes: If V8 ever formalizes an rsi_divergence expert it must be computed on log/ROC basis and treated as a gated confirmation signal, not a standalone entry; divergence as a reversal alone is high-risk per this book.

strategy_name: Single moving-average cross with breakout-entry filter (SMA vs EMA)
mechanism: Close-versus-MA is an objective trend division; a 1-tick breakout entry beyond the bar filters false signals; on tested FX data SMA performed at least as well as EMA
setup_summary: On EURUSD daily 1998-2007: if close > MA(n) buy at 1 pip above the bar high; if close < MA(n) sell at 1 pip below the bar low (filter for false signals). Parameter sweep of 10-21 days: best input is 13 days for both SMA and EMA; SMA slightly better (13-SMA: 250 trades, 33.2% profitable, win/loss 2.39, net profit $32,305 vs 13-EMA: 28.2%, $16,620). Weekly sweeps (4-12) similar with SMA more consistent. Classic trend-following payoff shape: ~30-40% win rate with win/loss ratio > 2.
trigger_invalidation: 'Moving average strategies get destroyed in range bound markets' — the method requires a trend/regime filter and is invalidated by whipsaw in ranges; switching methods after losses is explicitly warned against (consistency is the edge).
risk_geometry: Entry: stop-buy at high+1 pip (long) / stop-sell at low-1 pip (short) after the close crosses the MA; position is flipped on the opposite signal (no separate stop/target in the test).
quote: Buy when price crosses above the moving average and sell when price crosses below the moving average. There is no simpler trending strategy and it works well.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Moving Averages, pp. 109-112
notes: Corroborates V8's trend_pullback EMA signal. Adds: (1) 1-tick breakout entry filter, (2) SMA >= EMA on this data, (3) 13-period optimal on daily FX — all are testable refinements on BTCUSDT. The win-rate/win-loss structure is a useful prior for expected trend-following PnL shape in the simulator.

strategy_name: Pivot-zone breakout (Fisher pivot zones, tight-zone expansion)
mechanism: A pivot zone between PivotHigh and PivotLow concentrates reference levels; zone width encodes the prior period's close-location (tight zone = breakout ahead, wide zone = range ahead); buying above PH / selling below PL avoids whipsaw
setup_summary: Calculate PivotHigh (PH) and PivotLow (PL) from (H+L+C)/3 and (H+L)/2 (add/subtract their difference). If price is above the zone, take a bullish bias with a stop below the zone; enter only on a breakout above PH (buy) or below PL (sell). Zone width is informative: a tight zone warns of a breakout period; a wide zone indicates range-bound conditions. A rolling pivot zone (highest high / lowest low of the last x periods + last close) is used for trailing stops.
trigger_invalidation: Do not trade inside the zone ('by only playing breakouts from the pivot zone... you have a method to avoid frustrating whipsaw market action'); a breakout is invalidated if price re-enters the zone.
risk_geometry: Entry: stop-buy above PH / stop-sell below PL; stop: below/above the pivot zone; trailing: rolling pivot zone (book: 3-, 4-, 5-day; scalpers can try 12/24-hour).
quote: A tight pivot zone warns of a breakout period and a wide pivot zone indicates a higher probability of a range bound period.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 6, Pivot Zones and Rolling Pivot Zone, pp. 114-117
notes: Crypto perp is 24/7, so period boundaries are arbitrary — recompute zones on fixed UTC windows. Range compression followed by expansion is a documented BTC behavior; candidate expert or location/volatility feature feeding breakout_retest.

strategy_name: Elliott 1-2 Base deep-pullback entry (variant of trend_pullback)
mechanism: After a completed 5-wave impulse off a significant low/high, the wave-2 (or B) correction retraces roughly 50-61.8% and shakes out remaining crowd traders; shorts must cover, fueling the wave-3 (or C) explosion
setup_summary: Identify a completed 5-wave impulse from a significant high/low; on the ensuing 3-wave correction, wait for a retrace of ~50-61.8% (corrections off significant extremes 'usually retrace at least 50 percent of the preceding impulse, and often end near the 61.8 percent level'); enter half the position on the pullback and half via a stop above the wave-1 (or wave-A) extreme; stop below the origin of the impulse. Highest reward-to-risk when the impulse begins from a significant low/high; the trade is invalid if the correction retraces 100% of the impulse.
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if wave 2/B retraces 100% of wave 1/A (motive-wave rule) or if a triangle unfolds before wave 5 (stop gets triggered — book's own example of the flaw). Also a sharp wave-2 correction is a feature (more bears to cover), not a bug.
risk_geometry: Entry: half on the deep pullback (50-61.8% retrace), half stop-entry above wave-1 high / below wave-1 low; stop: below origin of wave 1/A; target: Fibonacci extension (wave 3 = 1.618 x wave 1; wave C = 1-1.618 x wave A).
quote: If the rally happened in five waves, then buy the ensuing correction (this is the 1-2 Base).
chapter_anchor: Ch. 7, Specific Setups — 1-2 Base, pp. 170-172
notes: Elliott counting is subjective and hard to make deterministic in V8; the falsifiable core is 'deep pullback (~50-61.8%) after a strong impulse, continuation through the impulse extreme'. This is a variant of the existing trend_pullback family (which currently uses a shallow close<ema_slow pullback) — a deep-retrace variant plus split entry is a candidate parameter-variant family.

strategy_name: Trend-following pullback entry (buy the dip / short the rally) with trailing stop below last swing
mechanism: Trends persist; countertrend retracements (dips in uptrend, rallies in downtrend) offer high-probability entries in the direction of the prevailing trend.
setup_summary: Identify an intact trend (higher lows/higher highs for uptrend via trendline or channel). Buy dips (temporary downward retracements) within the uptrend, or short rallies within the downtrend. Hold while the trend is intact; manage with a trailing stop moved to just below the last swing low; the break of the last swing low invalidates the uptrend thesis.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: retracement within a technically confirmed trend reaches support (trendline/channel floor or swing low). Invalidation: price breaks below the last swing low (uptrend) — trailing stop exits; trend-stage logic warns against late-stage entries when higher highs fail or volatility collapses.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar-close on dip/rally. Stop: below last swing low (manual trailing stop); alternatively below trendline/channel floor. Target: multiple R (reward-to-risk 'as high as possible', 'several times the magnitude of the initial stop loss'); trailing stop preferred over fixed profit target. Expiry: none — hold while trend intact. Scaling in/out (fractional positions) supported.
quote: trend traders generally prefer to enter into a trend at high probability locations within the trend... buying on the dips in an uptrend... selling short on the rallies.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Trend Trading—Going with the Flow', pp.140-146 (Exhibit 5.1, p.143)
notes: Directly corroborates the existing V8 trend_pullback expert (ema_fast>ema_slow + close<ema_slow, target_r 1.0/stop_r 1.0/expiry 8). Book suggests richer geometry for this family: trailing stop below last swing low rather than fixed ATR stop, and scaling in/out. 24/7 crypto: no gaps, 1h BTCUSDT trends well; whipsaw on late-stage entries flagged by the book's trend-stage discussion.

strategy_name: Moving average crossover system (single-price and 5/20 dual-MA variants)
mechanism: Moving average direction and crossovers describe the prevailing trend; price crossing a MA (or short MA crossing long MA) is a buy/sell signal; systems are typically always-in-market.
setup_summary: Price crosses above a single MA (e.g. 20) -> buy; crosses below -> sell. Or 5-period MA crosses above 20-period MA -> buy, below -> sell. Always-in-market: each opposite crossover closes the prior trade and opens the opposite one. Whipsaw losses are the known cost; profits must come from letting winners run in trending periods.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: crossover at bar close. Invalidation: opposite crossover; whipsaw strings in nontrending sideways markets are the expected failure mode (no trend filter).
risk_geometry: Entry: bar-close on crossover. Stop: none specified (always-in-market system; losses capped by opposite crossover). Target: let winners run. Whipsaw count is the main cost. Book's day-trading example adds filters: 14-RSI above 30 and rising MACD histogram as confirmation (explicitly 'not tested').
quote: If the shorter-period moving average crosses above the longer one, it would be considered a signal to buy. Conversely, if the shorter moving average crosses below the longer one, it would be considered a signal to sell.
chapter_anchor: Ch3 'The Magic of Moving Averages', pp.72-77 (crossovers pp.75-76); Ch5 'Day Trading' p.138
notes: Refines the existing trend_pullback family's trend filter (currently ema_fast>ema_slow) with an explicit always-in-market crossover variant. Book warns whipsaws are unavoidable — a regime/volatility filter (ADX mentioned p.89, p.141) is the natural guard. Applicable to 1h perps; taker-fee churn cost of repeated crossovers must be modeled in the simulator.

strategy_name: Breakout with pullback/throwback retest entry (breakout-hold-then-bounce)
mechanism: A true breakout carries directional momentum; if price retraces to the breakout level (pullback after down-break, throwback after up-break) and bounces off it, the break is confirmed and the retest is a higher-probability entry than the initial break.
setup_summary: Price breaks a horizontal support/resistance, trendline, pattern, or pivot level. Wait for the return to the breakout level (pullback/throwback). If price bounces at that level, enter in the breakout direction. Entering beyond the breakout point trades off false-break avoidance against early-entry profit.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: retest of a broken level that holds and bounces. Invalidation: price fails back through the breakout level — the break is declared false/premature and a hard stop (just before the breakout point) exits.
risk_geometry: Entry: on retest bounce (bar close). Stop: hard stop just before/below the breakout point ('right before the breakout point where... the price move will have proven itself to be a false or premature breakout'). Target: next support/resistance level; for all-time breaks, new extremes beyond the broken level. Patience cost: many true breakouts never retest.
quote: if the break is true (which means it carries real directional momentum) price should hit and bounce off the point of breakout, and then surpass the point at which breakout momentum waned and price turned.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Breakout Trading (and Fading)', pp.150-157 (pullback/throwback p.156)
notes: Corroborates the existing V8 backlog family breakout_retest (DATA_BLOCKED, location/volatility/history). Book adds concrete risk geometry: hard stop below the breakout point, target = next structure level. In 24/7 perps there are no exchange gaps, so retests of broken 1h levels are cleanly observable — no gap-fill ambiguity.

strategy_name: Horizontal range trading at support/resistance with minimum-range-height filter
mechanism: In nontrending markets price bounces repeatedly between horizontal support and resistance; entering at the boundaries with a stop beyond the boundary and a target at the far side has positive skew when the range is tall enough.
setup_summary: Establish a horizontal range with at least two approximate touches of both support and resistance (or Bollinger Bands with a flat/near-flat middle SMA). Enforce a minimum range height so the target far side justifies the stop risk (e.g. 20-pip GBP/USD Asian range not worth trading; 300-pip range is). Buy near support, sell near resistance; confirm turns with oscillator exits from overbought/oversold (Stochastics/RSI) or an intra-range trendline break.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price near range boundary + oscillator turn confirmation (crossing out of overbought/oversold). Invalidation: range broken (stop beyond the boundary level); flatness of the range violated.
risk_geometry: Entry: at/near boundary (bar close). Stop: just beyond the support/resistance level from which the trade is initiated. Target: other side of the range; a tighter stop is possible if an intra-range trendline break confirms the turn. Expiry: none stated; swings typically 1h-4h-daily timeframe.
quote: If stop losses are always placed just beyond the support or resistance level from which a range trade is initiated... a prudent range trading approach should include some minimum criteria for the height of the range.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Range Trading—Between a Rock and a Hard Place', pp.147-150
notes: New mean_reversion family with a falsifiable minimum-height filter. Crypto 1h ranges exist but trend phases dominate and range-breakout risk is elevated by leverage; the range-height threshold is the key testable parameter. No time-of-day bias claim (unlike FX session ranges); 24/7 market means no session-open boundary effects.

strategy_name: Bollinger Squeeze volatility breakout (contraction-to-expansion) with head-fake caution
mechanism: Volatility is cyclical: periods of high volatility follow periods of low volatility; when bands narrow dramatically (squeeze), the stage is set for a violent breakout in either direction — but a short fake-out move ('head fake') often precedes the real surge.
setup_summary: Observe Bollinger Bands (20-period SMA, 2 std) tightening to historically low bandwidth around a consolidating price structure. Expect an imminent expansion. Trade the eventual directional break, allowing for a possible head-fake fake-out first; manage risk so a fake-out does not stop the position out before the real move.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: band bandwidth at historical low + price structure consolidating. Invalidation: direction-agnostic — the trade must survive the head-fake; a clean expansion in the wrong direction invalidates the chosen side.
risk_geometry: Entry: on the post-squeeze breakout (bar close) with allowance for the fake-out. Stop/target: not specified by the book; V8 would add ATR-based stop and R-target. Expiry: none stated; squeeze resolution typically within a handful of bars on the trading timeframe.
quote: periods of high volatility generally follow periods of low volatility. When the Bollinger Bands narrow dramatically, volatility is drastically decreased. The subsequent expectation, then, is for price to breakout violently in either direction.
chapter_anchor: Ch3 Tips & Techniques 'The Bollinger Squeeze', p.91
notes: Volatility clustering is pronounced in crypto and the 24/7 market resolves squeezes without gap discontinuities, making the contraction-expansion pattern cleanly measurable on 1h BTCUSDT. The head-fake warning is a falsifiable sub-claim (fake-out precedes true break in a measurable fraction of squeezes). New expert family under complexity-budget rule 14.

strategy_name: Price-oscillator divergence as reversal timing signal
mechanism: When price makes a higher high while the oscillator makes a lower high (bearish divergence), price momentum is fading and a reversal is more likely; a few accurate divergences can offset many false ones because reversal entries are so profitable.
setup_summary: On the trading chart (book recommends longer timeframes for reliability), compare price swings with an oscillator (RSI, Stochastics, MACD). Bearish divergence: price higher high + oscillator lower high -> expect down move. Bullish divergence: price lower low + oscillator higher low -> expect up move. Book stresses divergence is a confirmation/hint tool, not a standalone strategy.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: confirmed divergence at a swing extreme. Invalidation: momentum resumes (divergence fails); no defined failure threshold in the book — V8 must add one (e.g., oscillator making a new extreme with price).
risk_geometry: Entry: at the swing extreme after divergence confirmation (bar close). Stop: beyond the swing extreme. Target: prior structure / swing; no R-multiple stated. Expiry: none.
quote: bearish divergence (which hints at an impending reversal back down) occurs when price hits a higher high while the oscillator hits a corresponding lower high.
chapter_anchor: Ch5 'Divergence Trading—Separate Paths', pp.170-172 (Exhibits 5.13/5.14)
notes: The book explicitly demotes divergence to a confirmation tool ('much less often are they employed exclusively as a full-fledged, self-sufficient trading strategy'), which argues for integrating it as a confirmation in the mean-reversion/range family rather than a standalone expert. Medium applicability on 1h perps; better on 4h+. Momentum as a feature group is absent from the frozen V8 vocabulary — divergence needs trend+response-style features.
book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

strategy_name: News/data trading on consensus deviation (expectation vs surprise), including secondary-reaction entry
mechanism: Price moves on the surprise, not the number: the market has already priced in the consensus, so trades are taken on how far actual data deviates from consensus; initial reactions are unreliable, so a secondary reaction (reversal or pullback-continuation) can be a cleaner entry.
setup_summary: Before a scheduled release (NFP, CPI, FOMC, GDP, retail sales, PMI, trade balance...), memorize consensus. When the actual print deviates from consensus by at least a trader-set threshold, trade in the direction implied by the deviation. Variant: skip the initial spike (deemed unreliable, with gaps/widening spreads) and enter on the secondary reaction — a full reversal of the initial move or a continuation after pullback/consolidation.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: |actual - consensus| >= threshold at release time. Invalidation: price already priced-in (a 'bad' number that rallies the dollar means consensus was worse); no clear deviation direction; whipsaw/nondirectional volatility is the known failure mode. Data revisions can move markets more than the original release.
risk_geometry: Entry: market order within milliseconds (speed variant) or bar-close on secondary reaction (patient variant). Stop: not specified; book notes spreads widen and price gaps occur in fast markets, so fills are less reliable. Target: 'a few pips' quick scalp or continuation of the one-way run. Expiry: seconds-to-minutes (scalp) for the speed variant.
quote: trading can take place based on how far the actual numbers deviate from the consensus numbers. In this way, news trading is based almost entirely on relative values rather than absolute values.
chapter_anchor: Ch4 'No News Is Bad News for News Traders' pp.121-124; Ch5 'News Trading' p.183
notes: The expectation-surprise mechanism transfers to crypto (scheduled US macro releases and FOMC move BTCUSDT at 1h scale; 24/7 trading means releases land in-session), but it requires a scheduled-release + consensus data feed absent from the V8 OHLCV tape and conflicts with deterministic replay (no wall clock, event/available/ingested clocks never collapsed). The secondary-reaction variant is the most implementable fragment and could inform a response-behavior feature.
book: Essentials of Foreign Exchange Trading 2009

strategy_name: Join-the-crowd trend continuation (DITM/ITM trade)
mechanism: a confirmed strong trend persists; buying the high-probability leg (deep in-the-money) monetizes persistence with a ~2% buffer against reversal
setup_summary: On 4h/day charts, confirm a strong trend via: price above the daily trend line in the trade direction, price through its 50-period MA, and a sequence of new daily highs (or lows), with trend-line angle ~37-45 deg. Buy the deep-in-the-money leg (premium $75-85, ~2% distance from spot) betting settlement stays on the trend side. Falsifiable on BTCUSDT 1h: after a streak of new N-bar extremes plus close > 50-EMA, P(close higher in next 24 bars) exceeds the premium-implied ~80% threshold.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: strong-trend confirmation (new-high streak + MA/trend-line alignment). Invalidation: trend fails to keep making new highs/lows; close back through the 50-period MA; dead-thesis if trend angle steepens past ~45 deg (overextension).
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close on confirmation; risk limited to premium; target = fixed $100 payoff (equivalent R ≈ 0.18-0.33R per trade, high win-rate); expiry = end-of-period (weekly in book -> 24-168 bars in V8); still_valid = trend persists.
quote: If the trend is strong and the headlines seem to be screaming at you... such conditions provide confirmation for an in-the-money strategy, which is a trend-following approach. ... a DITM trade makes a lot of sense.
chapter_anchor: Ch. 7 (pp. 128-129); trend checklist Ch. 5 (pp. 76-78)
notes: Same mechanism family as existing trend_pullback (trend_continuation); a new behavior variant (join-on-strength rather than buy-the-dip) with high win-rate/low-payoff geometry. Book's own week-2 occurrence analysis (Ch 2, p. 21) found buying everything priced >80% won that week, but warns it will not always work - exactly the evidence-bound caution V8 needs.
