strategy_name: Compression breakout (triangles, narrow channels, wedges)
mechanism: range compression squeezes sentiment into an apex; the subsequent expansion resolves the range, so a breakout leg placed outside the range wins
setup_summary: On 4h/30m charts, identify a triangle (ascending/descending/symmetrical), narrow sideways channel, or wedge where the high-low range narrows progressively; place a breakout leg just outside the range (buy above resistance / sell below support), betting settlement occurs outside the range. Strongest when timed to scheduled data releases (NFP, central bank statements) or after a doji cluster. Falsifiable: normalized range (e.g., (high-low)/ATR) below a threshold is followed by a range-expanding move within N bars.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: compression (range/ATR ratio falling across >=2 successive windows, e.g., triangle apex). Invalidation: price breaks then closes back inside the range (false break); expiry passes without the break.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close on range break; risk = premium (OTM leg $15-46 -> ~5:1-2:1 payoff); target = $100 payoff; expiry = end of week in book; direction-agnostic straddle variant allowed (breakout either way, same payout).
quote: Triangles can be considered preludes to breakouts. The binary option trader, when seeing a triangle, should locate the strike prices outside of the triangle and play a breakout. ... The breakout trade is essentially a play on volatility.
notes: Crypto perps are prone to range-compression-then-expansion on 1h; needs a definable compression measure (range/ATR or Bollinger width). Corroborated by the Bollinger 'narrow band = breakout precondition' claim (Ch 6, p. 99).
book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

strategy_name: Failed-breakout retry
mechanism: a range that has already resisted one breakout is range-exhausted; the next attempt is more likely to succeed because markets do not stay sideways indefinitely
setup_summary: After a breakout attempt fails (price breaks a range high/low then closes back inside), re-enter the breakout in the same direction on the next attempt at the same level. Book claim: 'if the previous week's breakout trade failed, the probability that the next one will work is actually greater.' Falsifiable: conditional on at least one failed break of level L, P(successful break within N attempts) versus unconditional base rate.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: prior failed breakout at level L (touch-and-close-back-inside) followed by a fresh approach to L. Invalidation: second failure closes deep inside range; the retry thesis dies if the range itself breaks on the far side.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close above (below) L; stop = back inside the range (structural); target = measured move / structure beyond L; expiry in bars; no premium analog in V8 (perps).
quote: Sometimes the trader is timing the breakout too early. In fact, if the previous week's breakout trade failed, the probability that the next one will work is actually greater because markets don't stay sideways too long.
notes: Distinct from V8's failed_breakout expert (which SHORTs the failure); this is the opposite leg - retry the break. Both could coexist as variants; test the 'failure increases next-attempt success probability' claim as an empirical conditioning question.
book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

strategy_name: Channel bounce / ATM bounce (mean reversion to mid-range)
mechanism: inside a defined channel, price oscillates between support and resistance; fading the extremes with a mid-range target monetizes the oscillation
setup_summary: On a sideways channel (or near a well-tested support/resistance zone), buy the bounce off the bottom / sell the bounce off the top, targeting the middle of the range. Book tactic: enter at $45-55 premium, close at a $75-80 objective (~77% return) rather than riding to expiration. Falsifiable: in a range regime, touch of a 3-touch S/R level followed by close back inside predicts a move back to range-mid within N bars.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: price probes a confirmed S/R level inside a range and shows a rejection close. Invalidation: price closes through the level (level breaks -> becomes supply_demand_zone role-switch signal instead); range regime degrades into trend.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close on rejection; stop = beyond the tested level (swing); target = mid-range or fixed R (~0.6R of the range width); expiry short (book: within hours-to-days).
quote: Bounce plays are in the lingo of technical analysis: mean reversion plays betting that the price will move back toward the middle of the range. ... A good method for a bounce trade is not to go to expiration but to select a target price to close the position.
notes: Requires a regime filter (range vs trend) to avoid fading trends; V8 has no active mean-reversion expert, so this is a genuinely new family candidate. The 'vibrating your way to profits' variant rides oscillation with strike mid-range.
book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

strategy_name: Support/resistance role-switch after break
mechanism: broken S/R flips polarity: tested-and-broken resistance becomes new support, so a pullback to the old level finds fresh buyers
setup_summary: Mark support/resistance with >=3 touches on 4h/day timeframes (higher timeframes = stronger evidence); after price breaks through, the old level flips role - buy the pullback to former resistance (now support) in an uptrend, or sell the rally to former support (now resistance) in a downtrend. Falsifiable: P(bounce at flipped level) > P(bounce at untested level), conditioned on >=3 prior touches.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: break and close through a 3-touch level, then price returns to the level. Invalidation: close through the flipped level (no bounce); fewer than 3 touches = weak level, do not trade.
risk_geometry: Entry: bar close at the flipped level; stop = beyond the level by an ATR cushion; target = prior structure / measured move; expiry in bars; book uses S/R to place the binary strike just above/below the level.
quote: When these events occur... the support line begins to act as a new resistance line. The resistance line begins to act as a new support line. ... Many traders use three touches to confirm that the lines are good lines to locate possible entry positions.
notes: Foundation pattern, likely corroborated by many books in the library; cleanly testable on 1h perps. Book couples it with Bollinger coincidence to strengthen level confidence (Ch 6, p. 101).
book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

strategy_name: Price-break persistence and streak exhaustion
mechanism: trend = persistence of new highs/lows; the streak length of consecutive new extremes measures trend strength, and streaks approaching their historical maximum signal exhaustion and a defined reversal level
setup_summary: Replace subjective trend lines with price-break (three-line break) charts: a new 1h/4h high paints a block, a new low paints a down block; no new extreme = nothing drawn. Trend strength = run length of same-direction blocks; a reversal block appears only if price gives back N previous extremes (3-line rule), so the reversal LEVEL is known in advance even if the time is not. Small new-extreme increments (small blocks) signal a tired trend and an impending breakout; streaks approaching the instrument's observed max block count (book example: ~21) signal likely reversal. Falsifiable: conditional distribution of streak lengths; P(reversal within K bars once streak >= local max).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: streak length reaches local historical maximum percentile, or reversal block prints (N prior extremes given back). Invalidation: streak extends beyond observed max (trend strengthens); small-block compression resolving as breakout continuation rather than reversal.
risk_geometry: Entry: on reversal block print or streak-max condition; stop = beyond the reversal block high/low; target = prior block cluster / Fibonacci-confluent level (book: fib lines often coincide with reversal points); expiry in bars.
quote: If a series is in place that is approaching 21 blocks, there is a high probability that a reversal is about to occur... Price break charts actually and precisely define and project where, not when, such a price reversal will appear.
notes: Directly implementable as a marketstate feature: count of consecutive new 1h extremes + its rolling percentile; feeds trend-strength scoring and a potential exhaustion-reversal expert. Book also uses it to match durations (1m-renko for 1m binaries etc., Ch 2 p. 25) - a timeframe-linking methodology V8 can borrow.
book: Trading Binary Options - Strategies and Tactics 2nd edition 2016

strategy_name: Bollinger Band mean-reversion (regression to the mean / Extended Bollinger Bands)
mechanism: overextension reverts: price touching the lower (or an extended) Bollinger Band in a non-trending market mean-reverts to the middle band
setup_summary: In a ranging market (no confirmed trend), when price touches and then closes back inside the lower Bollinger Band (or an Extended Bollinger Band for deeper overextension), go LONG targeting the middle band; mirror-short at the upper band. Falsifiable on 1h: price closes inside band after a band touch in a flat regime.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: band touch followed by close reclaim inside the band in a range regime. Invalidation: strong trend regime (trend feature says trending) or a band-walk where price rides the band without reverting.
risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after reclaim; stop beyond the touch bar extreme (or 1 ATR below low); target mid-band (0.5 R) or opposite band; expiry in bars bounded by mean reversion horizon; band width = ATR-based.
quote: Regression to the mean, 98; Price action on lower Bollinger Band, 104; Extended Bollinger Bands (EBB), 104-105, 106
chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 98-106 (Bollinger Bands, Low Bollinger Band, Extended Bollinger Bands)
notes: No exchange gaps in 24/7 perp makes a clean band-touch bar observable (no overnight gap past the band); needs a regime/trend feature gate to avoid catching trends (band-walks). This is the strongest new-family candidate from this book.

strategy_name: Breakout plays (range/consolidation break with event catalyst)
mechanism: consolidation break continuation: a decisive break of a range or prior high/low, especially with an event/volume catalyst, continues; failed breaks revert (feeds the existing failed_breakout family)
setup_summary: After sideways consolidation (or pre-event), a close beyond the range extreme with expansion triggers a continuation trade in breakout direction; the book documents FOMC-related breakout plays and lists breakout trades among high-risk performance challenges. Retest of the broken level validates; failure to hold the break = failed breakout (existing SHORT family).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close beyond consolidation extreme. Invalidation: close back inside the range (break failed) or rejection at the broken level = flip to failed_breakout.
risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE after break; stop back inside the range / 1 ATR; target measured move of the range (1R+); expiry tied to event follow-through.

strategy_name: Candlestick reversal/hesitation patterns (hammer, engulfing, doji, spinning tops, tweezers)
mechanism: reversal-candle context: specific candle shapes (hammer, engulfing, tweezers) after a trend, and hesitation candles (doji, spinning tops) at structure, mark potential reversal or pause points
setup_summary: Candle patterns alone are weak standalone signals; the book treats them as context/confirmation (hammer at support after a down-move, doji inside a triangle showing hesitation). V8 translation: candle-shape features (hammer/engulfing/doji at key levels) as confirmation inputs to existing experts, not new standalone experts.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: pattern appears at a significant level in the expected context. Invalidation: pattern fails (close through the pattern extreme); context (level, trend) absent.
risk_geometry: Feature-input only: adds confirmation strength to existing families; no own risk geometry.
quote: Hammer (candle pattern), 71; Engulfing candles (candle pattern), 73; Spinning tops (candle pattern), 72; Tweezers (candle pattern), 73; Doji (candle pattern), 80; doji shows hesitation, 92

strategy_name: Triangle/compression with hesitation (doji) before breakout
mechanism: compression-energy accumulation: consolidation (triangles: symmetrical/descending/equilateral) with hesitation candles (doji, spinning tops) compresses range and energy, setting up an expansion/breakout; doji after a move shows hesitation before continuation or reversal
setup_summary: Detect a triangular/range compression (declining range width over N bars) with hesitation candles inside; the compression resolves with an expansion breakout. Falsifiable: range-width compression quantified by ATR/range percentile, then breakout direction. Book: triangles + doji hesitation patterns (pp. 89-93), including parabolic patterns warning.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: compression state detected (range/volatility contraction). Invalidation: range expands without a directional break, or false break flips to failed_breakout logic.
risk_geometry: Compression is a pre-breakout state feature; entry follows the existing breakout family (close beyond compression extreme); stop inside the compression; target measured move.
quote: Triangles, 89-90; triangle and [doji], 90-93; Hesitation patterns, 90-93; Parabolic patterns, 93
chapter_anchor: Index: pp. 88-93 (patterns for trading analysis, triangles, hesitation patterns)
notes: Range compression is highly measurable on 24/7 perp (no gaps disrupt the compression); feeds the breakout/breakout_retest families as a precondition detector. Strong backlog candidate, corroborated across the library.

strategy_name: QMAC moving-average queue alignment trend filter
mechanism: a trend is only trustworthy when price and its moving averages fall in strict sequential order of alignment; any rally/retracement that occurs while the averages are out of sequence is expected to be short-lived
setup_summary: On a fixed timeframe compute a stacked set of MAs (book uses 50/90/200-day; short set 5/5/13). Bullish regime = close above shortest MA above next above longest (positive queue); bearish = exact reverse. Entry only when price and MAs are sequentially aligned after a disorderly phase; when averages are NOT in queue order, do not trust counter-trend rallies/corrections to persist (stand aside or treat as short-lived). Falsifiable: after a disorderly-alignment rally, price reverts within the swing horizon more often than after a queued-alignment rally.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = full positive/negative queue established; thesis invalidated when any MA breaks out of sequential order (e.g. 50-day crossing back below 90-day while queue was positive) or price closes through the shortest MA against the queue.
risk_geometry: Entry on bar close after queue confirmed; book gives no numeric stop but states longer-term MAs mark probable support/resistance zones usable to compute risk/reward against entries.
quote: whether the outlook of the market is bullish or bearish, price and its various multiple averages should fall in an orderly alignment
chapter_anchor: Ch 2 'Price and Moving Averages'; Ch 6 'Queuing Theory of Moving Average Crossovers (QMAC)'
notes: Core regime concept of the book; no optimization claimed ('parameters ... are not optimized'). Works on any continuous timeframe; 24/7 crypto has no session alignment to distort MA stacks. Natural V8 use: marketstate trend-alignment feature gating all entries.

strategy_name: higher-timeframe trend gating ('look at the weekly, trade on the daily')
mechanism: trades executed on the daily time frame have higher win probability when the next-higher time frame (weekly) is trending in the same direction and is not overbought
setup_summary: Before any daily entry check the weekly chart: (1) weekly momentum not overbought and not bearish, (2) weekly price vs moving averages at a support level gaining strength, (3) daily momentum shows a bullish reversal. Enter daily trades only when weekly and daily trend in tandem; all entries/exits executed from daily patterns. Falsifiable: daily signals taken while weekly momentum is bearish or overbought underperform daily signals taken in weekly alignment.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = daily bullish reversal while weekly trend positive; invalidated when weekly momentum turns bearish/overbought or weekly price closes below its supporting MA.
risk_geometry: In worked example: entry at next trading day open (or next bar close), protective stop at low of preceding bar, target sized to 3:1 reward/risk against weekly support/resistance, swing holding period of weeks.
quote: The rule is to trade in the trending direction of the next higher time frame of the daily price, that is, weekly
chapter_anchor: Ch 7 'Trade on Daily Signals'; Ch 2 'Combining the Four Dimensions'
notes: Maps directly to V8 lifecycle gating (trade only in direction of higher-timeframe regime) and to the one-exposure-per-direction rule. On BTCUSDT 1h the analogous stack would be 1h vs 4h/1D.

strategy_name: ADX trend-strength regime with peak-turn warning
mechanism: rising ADX indicates trend strengthening, a declining ADX indicates weakening trend, and a downward turn in ADX from an extreme peak presages a change in price trend
setup_summary: Use 14-period ADX as a regime filter: ADX crossing above ~20 = trending market (directional, either way); crossing below 20 = non-trending. Watch for ADX making an extreme high and turning down - this implies a change of trend strength and therefore a probable price-trend/direction change soon. Falsifiable: after ADX turns down from a multi-week peak, price trend direction changes within the next several bars more often than a baseline.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = ADX turns down from a high; invalidated if ADX resumes making new highs (trend strength restored).
risk_geometry: Filter/regime only; book explicitly warns ADX 'should not be used as a buy or sell signal' and lags by about 30 bars to establish.
quote: The turning of direction in the ADX implies that there is going to be a change of trend strength
chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Average Direction Index'
notes: Book recommends using a short ADX period and focusing on its peak turning points, and pairs it with the 50/90/200 MA stack (Ch 6 Fig 6.17).

strategy_name: minimum 3:1 reward-to-risk gate and per-position risk cap
mechanism: taking trades only when expected reward is at least three times the possible loss, and risking a bounded fraction of portfolio per position, preserves capital so that the trend edge compounds
setup_summary: For every candidate setup, measure the stop distance (risk) and target distance (reward) against the next-higher-timeframe support/resistance; require reward >= 3x risk before entering (worked example: a 1:3 ratio was rejected as 'no new position'). Cap per-position risk between 1% and 5% of portfolio value. Falsifiable: trades accepted with reward:risk < 3 underperform accepted trades on realized R-multiples.
trigger_invalidation: Gate condition; trade skipped when the ratio fails regardless of signal quality.
risk_geometry: Reward/risk computed from entry, stop, and target; 3:1 used because HK equities 'tend to go into consolidation after a rise of 30 percent' (30% reward vs 10% risk).
quote: Many professional traders do not take a trade unless the potential profit is at least three times greater than the possible loss
chapter_anchor: Ch 8 'Risk Management'; Ch 7 'Trade on Daily Signals'
notes: Maps to V8 RiskGate admission logic; 3:1 is a heuristic floor, not an edge claim.

strategy_name: volume-trend confirmation and price-volume divergence warning
mechanism: volume expanding with price confirms trend; price rising on falling volume signals weakening; price falling on rising volume signals more decline; volume on breakout separates true from false breakouts
setup_summary: Compare price trend to volume trend using fast/slow volume averages (book: 2-day vs 10-day). Uptrend valid while volume expands with rising price; expanding range + rising volume = aggressive continuation; contracting range with unimpressive volume = vulnerable to reversal; a narrow-range stall on heavy volume marks strong support/resistance. VZO variant: positive/negative volume flow, above 50% = positive; cross above 30% = entry signal, cross below 70% = exit signal. Falsifiable: breakouts accompanied by volume above its recent average outperform breakouts without it.
trigger_invalidation: Price-volume divergence (price advancing while volume trend declining) invalidates continuation.
risk_geometry: Confirmation/filter only; 'a single volume bar by itself will not be meaningful' - must be read against recent history.
quote: we want to see good volume on a breakout as confirmation of the entry/exit signals and to distinguish a true breakout from a false breakout
chapter_anchor: Ch 2 'Volume'; Ch 5 'Reading Volume' and 'Money-Flow Indicator'
notes: Crypto perp venues report volume but wash-trading can inflate it; use venue-quality caveat and prefer notional volume.

strategy_name: classic and hidden price-momentum divergence
mechanism: momentum oscillator failing to confirm price reveals hidden strength/weakness: classic divergence precedes reversal, hidden divergence (in trend direction) signals continuation and re-entry
setup_summary: Track a momentum oscillator (book uses ROC-type 10/21-period) against price. Bullish divergence: price makes a lower low while oscillator makes a higher low (accumulation) -> buy at oversold. Bearish divergence: price higher high, oscillator lower high -> sell. Hidden bullish: in an uptrend correction, price higher low while oscillator lower low = underlying strength, re-entry. Hidden bearish: in a downtrend, price lower high while oscillator higher high = exit. Multiple concurrent divergences strengthen the signal. Falsifiable: after a divergence is completed, price reverses from the extreme within the swing horizon more often than after no divergence.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = divergence completed at an oscillator extreme; invalidated if the oscillator confirms price on the next swing (no divergence).
risk_geometry: Entry on confirmation of reversal; stop beyond the extreme pivot; divergence warns of trend change but 'does not necessarily take place at the exact turning point'.
quote: The more divergences that are occurring, the more significant they become
chapter_anchor: Ch 3 'Divergence Patterns'; Ch 6 'Momentum Oscillator'
notes: Divergence detection is computable on 1h crypto bars; hidden-divergence continuation variant is the less-crowded edge candidate.

strategy_name: long-MA-slope-filtered crossover (Edwards & Magee Eight Rules)
mechanism: crossover signals between a fast and slow MA are only reliable when the slower MA is flat or turning in the new direction; a cross against a steeply sloped longer MA is a false signal
setup_summary: Buy when price or the 50-day average penetrates the 200-day average on the upside AND the 200-day is flattening or rising (Eight Rule 1/5 adapted); sell on the mirror downside penetration with the 200-day flattening or falling. Worked counter-example: two identical 50>200 Golden Crosses on the Shanghai index - the first (200-day flat/rounding) produced a bull run, the second (200-day in steep straight decline, MAs not queued, bearish diagonal) reversed the next day. Falsifiable: crossovers executed with the longer MA in steep adverse slope lose more than those with a flat/turning longer MA.
trigger_invalidation: Longer MA slope does not confirm the cross direction (steep in the opposite direction) or price retraces >61.8% of the prior decline at the cross.
risk_geometry: Entry on cross confirmation (bar close); stop at the recent swing; target at structure; a buffer (e.g. 57.5% line, or 10% band) can be used to avoid whipsaws.
quote: when the 50-day average crosses with the 200-day average, it is important to note the direction and slope of the 200-day average also
chapter_anchor: Ch 6 'Queuing Theory of Moving Average Crossovers' (Eight Rules; Golden/Dead Cross)
notes: Concrete falsifiable refinement of a moving_average_cross family: add longer-MA slope as a validity condition; rescales to 1h BTC (e.g. 50/200 on hourly bars).

strategy_name: neckline/range breakout patterns with volume and measured target
mechanism: a break of a structural neckline or range boundary with volume activates a reversal/continuation, and the broken level becomes support/resistance on retest; target is a measured projection
setup_summary: Double top: two peaks; activated when price declines below the low between the tops; target = distance from the high point to the neckline projected downward. Double bottom: must close above the intervening high point before acting; target projected upward by the same distance. Head and shoulders: complete when price breaks the neckline (line across the two troughs) with volume sharply higher on the break; target = head-to-neckline distance projected from breakout. Rectangle/box: consolidation between parallel support/resistance; breakout with volume = trend in breakout direction; pattern not complete until the breakout occurs; post-break the neckline becomes support (bullish) or resistance (bearish). Falsifiable: a neckline break with above-average volume follows through to the measured target more often than a break on weak volume.
trigger_invalidation: Price re-enters the pattern/back above the neckline after a bearish break (or below after bullish) - pattern fails.
risk_geometry: Entry on neckline break (bar close); stop inside the pattern or just beyond the neckline; target = measured head-to-neckline / height-of-range projection; volume on breakout is the key confirmation.
quote: A head and shoulders pattern is completed when prices break below the neckline

strategy_name: two-bar candlestick reversals at oscillator extremes
mechanism: single candles are meaningless; two-or-more-candle confirmation at overbought/oversold extremes flags reversals, and breakouts from these patterns are typically short-lived (~10 trading days)
setup_summary: At momentum extremes (oscillator overbought/oversold), a bullish engulfing, harami, hammer, or piercing line after a downtrend = buy setup; bearish engulfing, dark cloud cover, hangman, or evening star after an uptrend = sell setup. Hammer with a long lower shadow at the low of a long downtrend is the most dependable; confirm with the next bar (strong open/gap up) before entry. Harami: follow the break when the previous day's high/low is exceeded. 'A breakout from an engulfing pattern generally is short term, lasting no longer than 10 trading days.' Falsifiable: two-bar reversal patterns appearing at oscillator-extreme after a trend produce a reversal within 1-3 bars more often than the same patterns in mid-range conditions.
trigger_invalidation: Next-bar action fails to confirm direction (e.g. hammer followed by a down close).
risk_geometry: Entry on next-bar confirmation close; stop below the pattern extreme (shadow low); horizon ~10 bars for engulfing breakouts.
quote: Hammer with a long shadow shows that the bears have failed to push price lower and is more reliable, especially when its shadow is much longer than its body

strategy_name: Trade the Break (close-confirmed breakout with range-fraction stop)
mechanism: A close beyond a range boundary confirms momentum has resolved the supply/demand imbalance; counter-moves against a fresh breakout retrace at most partway into the prior range, so the stop can sit inside the range at a fixed fraction of its height.
setup_summary: On M15/M30, define support/resistance with at least two touches each side. Wait for a candle that CLOSES above resistance (long) or below support (short) - the breakout candle. Enter at the opening of the next candle. Stop at the 60% mark of the prior range measured from the broken level (e.g., 41-pip range -> stop 25 pips beyond resistance); two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R.
trigger_invalidation: No trade on a wick-only touch (close-based confirmation required); trade invalid if the computed stop lands inside the wrong geometry; dead thesis if price closes back inside the prior range.
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar-open after breakout close; stop at 60%-of-range mark beyond the broken level; dual targets 1R and 2R; no expiry stated (intraday M15/M30).
quote: When prices close above resistance, that candle is called the breakout candle. ... The stop loss is placed below the midpoint of the prior range because we do not expect prices to fall back below that point.

notes: Feeds the DATA_BLOCKED breakout_retest backlog family. strategy_name: Piranha (Bollinger band-touch mean reversion, range regime)
mechanism: In a range regime, price touching a band extreme reverts toward the mean; the tight stop loss doubles as the regime detector - a stopped-out trade signals the range thesis failed and a trend is starting.
setup_summary: On M5 GBP/USD, long when price touches the lower Bollinger band (MA12, dev 2), short when it touches the upper band; stop 10 pips, target 5 pips (2:1 risk-to-reward, so viability hinges on a high win rate). Do not trade during major U.S./U.K. news releases. If stopped, the book's rule is to look for the next trade in the opposite direction (a stopped range trade implies a trend started).
trigger_invalidation: Invalid in trending regimes (book: strategy 'fails badly when the market goes into a strong trend'); hitting the 10-pip stop invalidates the range thesis; avoid major news windows.
risk_geometry: Entry on band touch (market); stop 10 pips; target 5 pips (unfavorable 2:1 risk:reward); expiry: scalper holds minutes; ~15-20 opportunities/day.
quote: Long trades are taken when market prices touch the bottom band; short trades are taken when market prices touch the upper band.

strategy_name: Trend Bouncer (Bollinger-band pullback in trend)
mechanism: Trends move in waves; a pullback that retraces to the mean of the recent wave (Bollinger center MA12) after a band-extension offers an entry with the trend at better price, with the outer dev-4 band as a volatility-scaled stop.
setup_summary: On H1/H4, when price hits the upper Bollinger band (MA12, dev 2) in an uptrend and then pulls back to touch the center MA12, go long at the MA12 touch; stop at the lower band of the dev-4 Bollinger set; three targets at 1:1, 1:2, 1:3 R. Symmetric short for the lower band (example: NZD/USD H1 short, risk 46 pips / reward 138 pips).
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if price never reaches the dev-2 band (no momentum-wave confirmation) or never retraces to the center; stopped if the opposite dev-4 band is breached (wave deeper than expected); dead thesis if price closes beyond the band structure.
risk_geometry: Entry at center MA12 touch (market); stop at opposite dev-4 band (volatility-scaled, analogous to atr_ref); laddered targets 1R/2R/3R; expiry: swing 2-5 days.
quote: When the candlestick hits the upper band of Bollinger Bands (MA 12, Dev 2), it indicates an upward momentum, and we prepare to go long. As prices retrace back to the MA 12 (the center line of the Bollinger Bands), a significant retracement has occurred, and it is a good time to enter for a long trade.

strategy_name: Trend Rider (EMA cross with ADX momentum-exhaustion exit)
mechanism: A fast/slow EMA cross detects an early momentum change; trend strength (ADX) rising above a threshold then collapsing marks exhaustion, so the profit exit is a momentum-decay event rather than a price target, letting winners run (book example shows a 1:5.4 R trade).
setup_summary: On H1/H4, long when EMA12 crosses above EMA36, then enter when price pulls back to touch EMA12; stop at EMA36 (minimum 30 pips from entry); NO fixed profit target; exit when ADX14 rises above 40 and then falls back below 40. Symmetric short on the downside cross (example: AUD/USD H1, risk 38 pips / reward 155 pips).
trigger_invalidation: Entry skipped if price never returns to EMA12 (momentum runs without a pullback); stopped if EMA36 (or 30-pip minimum) is breached; the ADX-above-40-then-below event is the only profit exit.
risk_geometry: Entry at EMA12 touch after cross; stop at EMA36, min 30 pips; no fixed target - exit on ADX 40 round-trip; expiry: swing 2-5 days.
quote: Once the ADX crosses above 40 and comes back below, it is telling us that the momentum is losing steam and it's time to exit the trade.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 7 'Trend Rider', pp. 155-163
notes: Distinct from trend_pullback and trend_bouncer because there is NO fixed target: the exit is a momentum-decay event (ADX>40 then <40), which maps to a new behavior family (adx_exhaustion_exit) under a trend-exhaustion mechanism. strategy_name: Fifth Element (MACD histogram momentum confirmation)
mechanism: A MACD histogram sign flip indicates a momentum shift; requiring five consecutive same-sign histogram bars filters whipsaw sign flips and confirms the shift is sustained before entry, with a known future entry time (the 5th bar).
setup_summary: On H1/H4, after the MT4 MACD histogram switches from negative to positive, wait for four positive bars and enter long at the opening of the fifth bar; stop at the last low of the histogram (the last high for shorts); two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R. Symmetric for short (example: EUR/USD H4, risk 147 pips / reward 294 pips).
trigger_invalidation: Invalid if the histogram flips sign again before five bars accumulate (count resets - no trade); stopped if the last-histogram-extreme is breached; dead thesis if histogram sign reverts after entry.
risk_geometry: Entry next-bar-open on the 5th histogram bar; stop at the last swing extreme of the histogram (last low for longs); dual targets 1R/2R; expiry: swing.
quote: We wait for five positive bars on the histogram to confirm the momentum before entering a long trade on the fifth bar.

strategy_name: Power Ranger (trend-gated stochastic range trade)
mechanism: In a range forming after a trend, the stochastic locates the range extremes; gating the extreme trade by prevailing momentum (buy oversold only in uptrends) avoids fading the trend - the book's explicit warning against trading stochastic extremes without the gate.
setup_summary: On H1/H4, draw the prevailing trend line. In an uptrend, wait for stochastic %K and %D (10,3,3) to fall below 20, then go long when they cross back above 20; in a downtrend, go short when they exceed 80 then cross back below. First target at the 75% mark of the range, second beyond the range (breakout anticipation); the stop is sized at 1:1 R to the first target and MUST fall beyond the range extreme or the trade is declared invalid.
trigger_invalidation: Trade invalid if the computed stop does not sit beyond the range extreme (support for longs / resistance for shorts); never trade the stochastic extreme against the trend direction; dead thesis if the range breaks.
risk_geometry: Entry on stochastic cross back out of the extreme zone (20/80); stop = 1:1 R to first target and must clear the range extreme; two targets (75% of range, then range extension); expiry: swing.
quote: Always determine the momentum of the market first before deciding whether to look for the overbought or oversold region of the stochastic. In an uptrend, look for the oversold region.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 10 'Power Ranger', pp. 177-185
notes: The transferable insight is the trend gate: buying oversold in a downtrend 'can be risky' (the book names it as the failure mode of naive stochastic trading). The second target beyond the range anticipates breakout, combining range fade with a breakout continuation in one position.

strategy_name: Queuing Theory of Moving Average Crossovers (MA-stack trend regime)
mechanism: When price and a stack of longer-period MAs align in sequential order (shortest above longest), the market is in a durable trend regime; when the stack is unaligned, any rally or retracement is short-lived.
setup_summary: On the daily timeframe, enter LONG when price closes above the 50-, 90-, and 200-day moving averages AND the MAs are stacked in sequential bullish order (shortest above mid above longest); enter SHORT on the mirror image. If price and MAs are not aligned in sequential order, do not expect new trend entries (any short-term rally/retracement is short-lived).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: close above all three MAs with bullish stack order. Invalidation: price closes back below the long MA or the stack order breaks (short MA crosses below mid MA).
risk_geometry: Entry at bar close after MA-stack confirmation. No stop, target, or expiry stated in this part (back-matter only); treat as a regime/trend filter rather than a full trade recipe.
quote: A bullish market is initiated when price crosses above its respective averages (e.g., 50-day, 90-day, and 200-day moving average lines) and the moving averages also follow in a sequential order with the shorter period moving average crossing above the longer period.

strategy_name: Price/oscillator divergence as trend-reversal signal
mechanism: When price's directional movement disagrees with the oscillator's, the impulse is losing internal confirmation; divergence generally indicates an impending trend reversal.
setup_summary: With any momentum oscillator (index references MACD, momentum oscillator, Blau's Momentum Direction and Divergence, plus hidden bullish/bearish divergence): price makes a higher high while the oscillator makes a lower high (bearish divergence) in an uptrend, or price makes a lower low while the oscillator makes a higher low (bullish divergence) in a downtrend; expect a trend reversal.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: divergence of oscillator extreme vs price extreme on the same leg. Invalidation: price breaks beyond the prior price extreme (divergence denied) or oscillator crosses back through the level of its prior divergence extreme.
risk_geometry: Not stated in this part; book treats divergence as a warning ('generally indicates trend reversal') needing confirmation, not an instant entry.
quote: Divergence occurs when the directional movement of the price disagrees with that of the oscillator. Divergence generally indicates trend reversal.

strategy_name: Outside-day range expansion / inside-day momentum-waning
mechanism: A day whose range engulfs the prior day's range represents a range expansion; the market tends to continue in the direction of that day's close. An inside day after a large move signals momentum is waning.
setup_summary: On the daily bar, if today's high-low range fully contains the previous day's range (outside day), expect the following move in the direction of today's close (LONG if the close is in the direction of the breakout leg, SHORT otherwise). Conversely, an inside day (today's range inside yesterday's) is a consolidation signal, and after a big prior move indicates waning momentum for that move.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: full engulf of prior day's range. Invalidation: subsequent bars fail to follow the outside day's close direction and price closes back inside the prior day's range.
risk_geometry: Entry in direction of outside-day close; no stop/target/expiry stated in this part.
quote: A day in which the previous day's price range is within the range of today's price range. This is often a signal that the market is about to make a move in the direction of the close.

strategy_name: Volume confirms price-move validity
mechanism: Volume and price agreeing (volume rising together with price) validates the move; the book's applied systems use a Volume Zone Oscillator and volume-ratio-compressed indicator to gauge this participation.
setup_summary: A trend move is considered valid/confirmed only when accompanied by rising volume (price up + volume up in an uptrend; price down + volume up in a downtrend); a move on flat or falling volume is treated as suspect. Volume zone oscillator and money-flow indicators are the book's operationalizations.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: directional move with expanding volume. Invalidation: new price extreme printed on contracting volume (confirmation absent).

strategy_name: Never-trade-against rule + MA failure in sideways markets
mechanism: The prevailing trend (HH/HL or LH/LL) defines the tradable regime; trading against it is disallowed, and indicator-based signals (especially moving averages) are unreliable in sideways/non-trending regimes.
setup_summary: Define the regime by higher highs/higher lows (uptrend) or lower highs/lower lows (downtrend); only take entries in the direction of that regime (never-trade-against rule). In a sideways/non-trending regime (no HH/HL or LH/LL), suppress signal-driven entries because moving averages behave as lagging indicators there.

strategy_name: Double top (M) / double bottom (W) reversal
mechanism: A double top is 'generally caused by flats' and a double bottom by 'failures' - the second peak/trough failing to exceed the first marks rejection of the prior trend and a reversal away from the range.
setup_summary: In an uptrend, price prints two conspicuous peaks at a similar level (double top, 'M'); if the second peak fails to exceed the first, anticipate a reversal (SHORT). Mirror for double bottom ('W') in a downtrend (LONG on the failure to make a new low).
trigger_invalidation: Trigger: second test of the prior extreme fails to exceed it. Invalidation: price breaks above the first peak (for the top) / below the first trough (for the bottom), negating the failure premise.
risk_geometry: Not stated in this part; conventional geometry would place stops beyond the pattern extreme, but the book text here gives none.
quote: Double top is generally caused by flats, double bottom by failures. Also known as 'M' and 'W' patterns.

strategy_name: Gap types: breakaway/common/runaway/exhaustion
mechanism: A day whose range sits entirely above or below the prior day's range creates a gap; the indexed taxonomy (breakaway, common, runaway, exhaustion) classifies gaps by position in the trend, each with distinct follow-through or fill behavior.

strategy_name: Upthrust (failed breakout of resistance)
setup_summary: During an uptrend, price breaks through an important resistance area, fails to hold the new highs, and pulls back under the previously pierced resistance. Enter SHORT on the close back below the pierced level.
trigger_invalidation: Trigger = close back under the pierced resistance; thesis invalid if price closes back above the reference (breakout level reclaimed).
risk_geometry: Entry NEXT_BAR_CLOSE; stop above the failed-breakout extreme; freeze the pierced-resistance reference (per V8 convention); exit on R-multiple target or dead-thesis.

strategy_name: Three-line break chart trend-reversal system
setup_summary: On a time-independent three-line break chart: a decline has started when the low of the last three rising lines is broken on the downside (sell / white-to-black turnaround); a decline has ended when the highest price of the last three declining lines is exceeded on the upside (buy / black-to-white turnaround). Variants: 'black shoe / white suit / neck' trades, record sessions, and uptrend support lines (Index p.174-190).
trigger_invalidation: Reversal requires breaking the extreme of the last three opposite-direction lines; moves smaller than that are ignored by construction; book acknowledges whipsaws in ranging markets (Index p.184).

strategy_name: Candlestick reversal signals require a prior trend (trend gate)
setup_summary: Candle theory: most candle signals are reversals, so a pattern or candle line only has meaning with a prior trend to reverse. A doji in the middle of a trading zone is not a trading signal; the same physical candle (hammer vs hanging man) is bullish or bearish purely on the direction of the prior trend.

strategy_name: Payoff asymmetry, not win rate, is the engine of successful trend trading
mechanism: Successful traders often lose more trades than they win; edge resides in letting winners run so the average winner exceeds the average loser (R:R > 1), not in forecast accuracy.
setup_summary: Design inference from the book's claim that 'many successful traders place more losing trades than winning trades': trend-following experts should be designed and evaluated as payoff-asymmetry systems (many small losses, fewer large gains). Implication for V8 trend-family geometry: target_r/stop_r asymmetry is a first-order design variable, and low win rate must not be treated as a defect.

strategy_name: Window (gap) continuation: reaction stops within window, close-through voids trend
mechanism: an unfilled window stores directional pressure; a close through it voids the prior trend
setup_summary: Detect a rising window (current bar low above prior bar high) or falling window. The trend is presumed to continue; a pullback that holds inside the window (no close through the far edge) is the entry. Rising window: long on a pullback close that stays above the window bottom; falling window symmetric short. If the window is not filled within three bars, that confirms continuation.
trigger_invalidation: A close through the far edge of the window voids the trend thesis; intra-session wicks through do not count. After 3 consecutive windows in one direction the market is 'overextended' - offset positions, do not add; only go countertrend after the last window is filled on a close.
risk_geometry: Entry at bar close (pullback into window or continuation); stop on a close through the window far edge; targets come from other tools (change-of-polarity levels, prior S/R) since candles give no targets; ~3-bar expiry for window-fill confirmation.
quote: The reaction will go until the window... if the price closes through the window, I then view the prior trend as being voided.

notes: On 24/7 BTCUSDT 1h, bar-to-bar windows are intermittent (continuous auction, overlapping ranges), so signal frequency is low on the most liquid pair but higher on alt perps and higher timeframes. strategy_name: Three-line break trend regime with turnaround lines
mechanism: a close beyond the far extreme of the last three same-direction closes flips the trend regime
setup_summary: From closing prices, add a white line on a new high and a black line on a new low; once three consecutive same-color lines exist, a reversal requires a close beyond the low of the last three white lines (black turnaround) or beyond the high of the last three black lines (white turnaround). Three white lines = bull regime: use bullish candle signals as longs and treat bearish candle signals as cover-only; a black turnaround line flips the regime to bear. Regime changes are close-confirmed and lag, so scale in lightly intra-session and add on confirmation.
trigger_invalidation: An opposite turnaround line flips the regime; 8-10 consecutive same-color lines mark overextension (record-session concept) and warn of a bounce.
risk_geometry: No explicit stops in the book; the turnaround line / last-three-lines extreme is the structural level; exits on the opposite turnaround.
quote: once three consecutive white or black lines appear... the market is in a trending mode. A basic trend reversal signal is produced when a turnaround line moves under three consecutive white lines or above three consecutive black lines.
chapter_anchor: Ch.6 'Three-Line Break Charts', pp.167-190
notes: Deterministic and close-only, so it ports cleanly to V8 replay. The book uses it explicitly as a trend filter for gating candle entries - a REGIME_FILTER role. Sensitivity adjusts from 2-line (faster) to 5/10-line breaks. 'Black shoe / white suit / neck' is a buy-on-second-confirmation variant of the turnaround signal.

strategy_name: Kagi yang/yin: buy on line-thickening, sell on line-thinning, with shoulders/waists and midpoint rule
mechanism: penetration of a prior extreme flips the line's structural state (thin/thick), marking a regime control change
setup_summary: Build a kagi chart with a fixed or percentage reversal amount (3% is the NTAA-expert default, 5% for longer-term). Buy when the line turns thick (yang - a thin line penetrated the prior high/shoulder); sell when it turns thin (yin - a thick line broke a prior low/waist). Rising shoulders plus rising waists = healthy bull; first lower shoulder or lower waist = weakening. A pullback holding above the midpoint of a long kagi line is bullish; a rally failing to pierce the midpoint in a downtrend is bearish.
trigger_invalidation: Opposite line-thickness change; a two- or three-level break provides extra confirmation at the cost of later entries.
risk_geometry: Structural stop below the last waist (longs) / above the last shoulder (shorts); midpoint of long kagi lines acts as support/resistance; intraday kagi (e.g., 5-minute) is explicitly supported.
quote: the most basic is to buy when the kagi line goes from thin to thick, and to sell when the kagi line changes from thick to thin.
chapter_anchor: Ch.8 'Kagi Charts', pp.213-239
notes: Fully computable and deterministic from closes; a percentage reversal auto-scales to BTC's changing volatility where fixed-dollar reversals would not. Folded-in sub-mechanisms: shoulders/waists structure, yang-vs-yin length comparison, midpoint support of long lines, double-window reversal patterns, tweezers (double top) and three-Buddha (head-and-shoulders) on kagi.

strategy_name: Record sessions: 8-10 new extremes = overextension, countertrend caution
mechanism: trend extension beyond ~8-10 new extremes exhausts the overbought/oversold condition, raising reversal odds
setup_summary: From a confirmed low, count record highs: each new high (including the upper shadow) is one record session; 2-3 sideways sessions between records are tolerated but a sharp countermove resets the count. After 8-10 record highs, stop adding longs and take a bearish candle signal there as a short/liquidate signal. Mirror with 8-10 record lows. The count is a guidepost - some markets turn at 6, others at 12.
trigger_invalidation: A sharp 2-3 session countermove or lateral relief of the overbought condition resets the count; do not go countertrend without a candle signal.
risk_geometry: No explicit stop in the book; relies on the confirming candle signal's structure; the count is deliberately non-consecutive.
quote: when there are eight to ten record sessions (that is, eight to ten almost consecutive higher highs or lower lows), it increases the possibility that the preceding trend will change.
chapter_anchor: Ch.3 'Record Sessions', pp.121-126; reused in Ch.6 and Ch.8
notes: Deterministic and cheap to compute; the same count extends to kagi shoulders/waists and three-line-break lines. 24/7 trading produces many new highs/lows, so the count fires frequently on 1h BTC - a natural overextension feature for the trend group.

strategy_name: Trend Rider (EMA12/36 pullback with ADX momentum-exhaustion exit)
mechanism: After a momentum-confirmed trend shift, buy the pullback to the fast EMA and ride until momentum exhausts; no fixed target prevents premature profit-taking
setup_summary: On H1 or H4, wait for EMA12 to cross above EMA36 (long bias). Enter long when price pulls back to touch EMA12. Stop at EMA36 (minimum 30 pips from entry). No predetermined profit target; exit when ADX(14) crosses above 40 and then drops back below 40.

risk_geometry: Entry on EMA12 touch (next-bar); stop at EMA36, minimum 30 pips; target = ADX-40 exhaustion exit (no fixed R); no fixed expiry; book example achieved 1:5.4 R.
quote: Once the ADX crosses above 40 and comes back below, it is telling us that the momentum is losing steam and it's time to exit the trade.

strategy_name: Piranha (Bollinger band-touch scalping with regime-flip-on-stop rule)
mechanism: In a range, price touching the outer Bollinger band reverts toward the mean; a stop-out at the band is itself a regime signal that the market has left the range and begun trending
setup_summary: On M5 GBP/USD with Bollinger Bands (MA 12, Dev 2), go long when price touches the lower band and short when it touches the upper band. Stop 10 pips, target 5 pips (risk:reward 2:1, negative expectancy per-trade compensated by high frequency). Avoid trading during major US/UK news releases.
trigger_invalidation: Stop-out indicates the band is no longer holding; the next trade should be the OPPOSITE direction of the stopped-out trade.
risk_geometry: Entry on band touch (market order at touch); stop 10 pips fixed; target 5 pips fixed; no expiry.
quote: hitting a stop loss is a telltale sign that the market is no longer trading in a band and it is starting to move into a trend.

strategy_name: Trade the Break (close-confirmed breakout with in-range 60% stop)
mechanism: A candle CLOSE beyond resistance/support is the market's confirmation that momentum is sufficient to continue; the stop placed deep inside the prior range survives the common whipsaw back into the range
setup_summary: On M15/M30, define support/resistance from at least two swing highs and two swing lows. When a candle closes above resistance (breakout candle), enter long at the open of the next candle. Place the stop at the 60% mark of the prior range BELOW resistance (i.e., deep inside the range). Two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R. Short mirror at support.
trigger_invalidation: Stop (60% into range) hit; opposite-side close breaks the level first.
risk_geometry: Entry at next-bar open; stop at 60% of range measured from the broken level into the range; targets 1R and 2R.
quote: The stop loss is placed below the midpoint of the prior range because we do not expect prices to fall back below that point.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 7, Strategy 4 (Trade the Break), pp. 131-137
notes: Distinct from the V8 backlog breakout_retest (no retest wait - enters next bar after close confirmation). strategy_name: Commodity Correlation (oil->CAD/JPY; Dollar Index->gold XAU/USD)
mechanism: Commodity price action leads a correlated currency: oil breaks out -> CAD/JPY follows (positive correlation, Canada net oil exporter, Japan net importer); Dollar Index breaks support -> gold rallies (inverse correlation)
setup_summary: On D1, use the lead instrument's support/resistance: if a candle closes above oil resistance, go long CAD/JPY at the next day's open; if a candle closes below Dollar Index support, go long XAU/USD at the next day's open (inverse). Stop at 2x ATR of the prior candle; target at 1:3 R.

strategy_name: Fifth Element (MACD histogram 5-bar momentum confirmation)
mechanism: A MACD-histogram sign flip is only reliable once confirmed by N consecutive same-sign bars; the delayed 5th-bar entry filters false flips and makes the entry time predictable
setup_summary: On H1/H4 with MT4-style MACD (12,26,9): when the histogram flips negative->positive, wait for four positive bars, then enter long at the OPEN of the fifth positive bar. Stop at the last histogram-swing low. Two targets at 1:1 and 1:2 R. Short mirror on positive->negative flip.
trigger_invalidation: Histogram re-crosses to the prior sign before five bars accumulate.
risk_geometry: Entry at 5th-bar open; stop at last swing extreme of the histogram; targets 1R and 2R.
quote: We wait for five positive bars on the histogram to confirm the momentum before entering a long trade on the fifth bar.

strategy_name: Power Ranger (trend-aligned stochastic pullback in a forming range)
mechanism: In an uptrend, an oversold stochastic reading is a pullback to buy, not a reversal signal; entry at the stochastic re-cross, with the admission gate that the stop must sit beyond the range edge
setup_summary: On H1/H4, establish trend direction from a series of higher highs/higher lows (long bias). In an uptrend, when stochastic %K/%D go below level 20 and cross back above 20, enter long; short mirror in a downtrend with level 80. TP1 at the 75% mark of the range; stop at 1:1 R; TP2 at 1:2 R beyond the range (anticipating breakout). Trade is INVALID if the computed stop is not below support (longs) / above resistance (shorts).
trigger_invalidation: Stop would sit inside the range (invalid trade); stochastic re-cross fails to trigger.
risk_geometry: Entry on stochastic re-cross; stop 1R and must be beyond the range edge; TP1 at 75% of range; TP2 at 1:2 R beyond range.
quote: In an uptrend, look for the oversold region. In a downtrend, look for the overbought region.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 8, Strategy 10 (Power Ranger), pp. 177-184
notes: The key transferable rules: (1) never trade the oscillator signal against trend momentum (buy oversold in uptrend only); (2) the invalidation gate - stop must be beyond the range edge or the trade is skipped - is a clean, deterministic admission rule for V8.

strategy_name: Guppy Burst (quiet-window range breakout via dual pending stops)
mechanism: Volatility compression during a quiet session window precedes expansion; the compression-range edges act as objective breakout triggers, and the mechanical pending-order structure removes timing discretion
setup_summary: On M5 GBP/JPY, in the ~3-hour window after the US market closes (before Asia opens), record the range: highest high = resistance, lowest low = support. Place a pending buy stop at resistance and a pending sell stop at support. TP = 2x the range distance (1:2 R). When one trigger fires, immediately cancel the other pending order.
trigger_invalidation: Opposite pending order triggers first; window expires without a trigger.
risk_geometry: Pending stop entries at range edges; stop at the opposite edge; TP 2x stop distance; intra-window expiry.
quote: The guppy burst seeks to identify the trading range during this 3-hour window and anticipate a potential breakout of the trading range.

strategy_name: Rule of 20 news trading (Gawk the Talk / Balk the Talk)
mechanism: Markets price expectations, not levels; only surprises beyond a deviation threshold move price in the direction of the deviation, so trade actual-vs-forecast deviations, not the number itself
setup_summary: Around scheduled news on M15/M30, compare actual vs forecast. If actual exceeds forecast by >=20% (special cases: PMI >=50 bps; interest rates >=20 bps), trade the affected currency in the direction of the deviation - long if the affected currency is the base, short if it is the counter currency. Stop 20 pips, target 40 pips. Short (Balk the Talk) when actual falls short of forecast by >=20%.
trigger_invalidation: Deviation below the 20% threshold - no trade (previous and forecast values alone carry no weight).
risk_geometry: Entry after release (next candle); stop 20 pips; target 40 pips (1:2 R).
quote: If the deviation between the actual and forecasted figures exceeds 20%, trade in the direction of the deviation.

strategy_name: Swing Rule Projection
mechanism: swing symmetry target projection: the retracement height from a swing peak to the pullback valley projects the height of the next swing in the trend direction
setup_summary: In an uptrend (daily bars), take the drop from peak 1 to valley 2 (height X) and add it to peak 1 to get the target for the next rise: e.g. A peaks at 29.17, B bottoms at 25.02 (height 4.15), target 33.32, actual peak 32.83. Mirror for downtrends by subtracting the rise height from the peak. Falsifiable: in the book's 2000-2011 US-equity test (32,042 up-trend / 24,620 down-trend samples) the target landed within +/-5 percent of projection 80% of the time in uptrends (86% for swings under 10% in height), 67% in downtrends (78% for small swings).
trigger_invalidation: Projection is invalidated when price reverses before reaching the symmetry target (undershoot) or overshoots through it; accuracy degrades for swings larger than about 10% in height.
risk_geometry: Target-only method: the book specifies no entry/stop/expiry; target = peak + prior retracement height (minus for shorts); the most reliable inputs are small swings (<10%).
quote: In up trends, it accurately predicts when price is going to peak 80 percent of the time.
chapter_anchor: Chapter 28 'Swing Rule' (pp. 299-302)
notes: Measured on daily US equities, so the 80% hit-rate is instrument-specific and must be re-tested on BTCUSDT. In 24/7 perps swing points form continuously with no session gaps, so the projection is computable on any bar size. Best V8 use: a target-projection feature to refine risk_geometry target selection rather than a standalone entry expert.

strategy_name: Chart Pattern Breakout Hold
mechanism: pattern breakout continuation: an upward breakout from a completed chart pattern starts a position held until a different chart pattern breaks downward or the structure stop is hit
setup_summary: Buy when price closes above a chart-pattern boundary (17 pattern types tested; ascending and symmetrical triangles excluded as buy signals, used only for exits). Place a stop a penny below the bottom of the pattern, hold until a downward breakout from another chart pattern or the stop, with no trailing stop. Tested on 500 stocks: 1,333 in-sample trades (win/loss 59%, avg +27%, avg hold 325 days) and 4,185 out-of-sample (win/loss 48%, avg +25%, avg hold 254 days).
trigger_invalidation: Close back below the pattern bottom after the breakout (bust or stop); worst observed trade was -72% when a tall double bottom retraced through the pattern.
risk_geometry: Entry = breakout bar close; stop = one tick below the pattern bottom (structure stop, not ATR); no trailing; exit = next pattern downward breakout or stop; hold horizon measured in months (254-325 days).
quote: Buy when the stock breaks out upward from a chart pattern... place a stop loss order a penny below the bottom of the chart pattern. Hold until price breaks out downward from another chart pattern or price hits the stop.

strategy_name: Trendline Break Requires 1-2-3 Confirmation
mechanism: a single close through a trendline is insufficient evidence of trend change; reversal is confirmed only by the first counter-trend peak and valley (1-2-3 sequence)
setup_summary: When price closes below an up-trendline (or above a down-trendline), do not declare a trend change on that bar; require the 1-2-3 sequence: first lower peak then first lower valley to confirm an uptrend reversal, first higher peak then first higher valley to confirm a downtrend reversal (the book's Test Yourself marks the 'higher peak + higher valley = change' reading as False). Related: triangle trendlines extended into the future act as future support/resistance areas (apex pivots), a location feature.

strategy_name: Measure Rule Pattern-Height Target
mechanism: pattern-height projection: the chart pattern's height (highest peak minus lowest valley) projected from the breakout level estimates the post-breakout move
setup_summary: For a descending triangle with a downward breakout: target = value of the bottom trendline minus the pattern height. Price reaches or exceeds that target only 42% of the time (book stat). The measure rule is applied across many patterns (triangles, double tops/bottoms, H&S, rectangles, flags/pennants, triple tops), making it a general structure-target method; the ch. 29 day-trader use is 'enter on pattern breakout, exit at the measure rule target.'

risk_geometry: Target = structure-projected price level; entry/stop are not specified by the rule itself.
quote: Subtract the height from the value of the bottom trendline to get a price target. Price reaches or exceeds the target 42 percent of the time.

strategy_name: FX-Ed Trend Technique (10-day EMA pullback in strong trend)
mechanism: institutional traders add positions at the 10-day EMA during runaway trends, so pullbacks to the EMA become high-probability continuation entry points; the longer the trend the more self-sustaining it becomes
setup_summary: Daily chart: moving averages in 'proper order' (10>20>50>200 SMA/EMA for an uptrend, reversed for a downtrend) AND price has been above (uptrend) / below (downtrend) the 10-day EMA for at least 10 consecutive candles (the filter proving the EMA genuinely acts as support/resistance). Enter long when price dips to the 10-day EMA in an uptrend, short on a rally to it in a downtrend. Initial stop = 50% of daily ATR(14) beneath the EMA; trail the stop once per daily close, never lower it; no target — exit only when the trailing stop is hit.
trigger_invalidation: No trade if MAs are not in proper order, or price cuts the 10-day EMA back and forth (EMA not acting as support/resistance); thesis invalid when a daily close breaches the trailed stop (0.5*ATR under the moving EMA).
risk_geometry: Entry at EMA touch (no candle-close wait); initial stop = 0.5*ATR(14) daily below EMA; stop trailed once per daily close under the moving EMA; no fixed target (let winners run); optional partial exit at the upper channel line with the remainder trailing.
quote: there is considerable evidence that in extremely strong trends, pullbacks (in the case of an uptrend) or rallies (in the case of a downtrend) to the 10-day exponential moving average make particularly effective entry points for forex traders. This is because the big players are using this moving average to determine their entry points as well.

strategy_name: Multiple time frame strategy: higher-TF direction gate + oscillator neutral-flip entry + soft-target partial exits
mechanism: trends persist across time frames, so trading only with the higher-timeframe direction and buying pullbacks (never entries at extremes) stacks probabilities; an oscillator leaving overbought/oversold back to neutral signals the counter-move has begun
setup_summary: Daily chart trending (trendline, ADX, or proper-order MAs) -> trade ONLY in that direction; reject all counter-trend setups. On the hourly chart, enter long when price pulls back to prior hourly support or to a Fibonacci retracement (38.2/50/61.8%) of the daily move that coincides with a prior S/R level, AND a 14-period RSI (or slow stochastic) has flipped from overbought back into neutral territory. Stop above the recent swing high and above the Fibonacci level.
trigger_invalidation: No trade if no discernible daily trend (technique is for trending markets only); never enter on the oscillator signal alone without the price-level confluence; invalid for shorts if price makes a new high beyond the stop level.
risk_geometry: Entry at Fibonacci/prior-support confluence when RSI crosses back to neutral; stop above recent high and above the Fibonacci level; exits: partial at 1R with stop moved to breakeven, remainder at prior support levels; book's 'soft target' tweak: raise S/R-based exits by ~10% of the support-resistance range so exits land ahead of round numbers and above the bottom of support.

notes: Adds two refinements to the existing trend_pullback family: (1) a hard higher-TF direction gate (phantom-signal discipline - do not take counter-trend setups even when they 'would have worked'), and (2) the 'overbought does not equal sell' rule - wait for the oscillator to flip to neutral before entry, sacrificing the exact top/bottom for confirmation. Its exit scheme (partial at 1R -> stop to breakeven -> remainder at prior support, with soft targets) is the book's recurring lifecycle pattern and is a candidate lifecycle_rule refinement for V8.
